item.title: 让游戏里的NPC记住你，到底要花多少钱？
item.description:
来源：游戏陀螺（中文） 相关度：27.3 正文：4319 字 / 21 图

命中：npc、渲染、dlss

在《星布谷地》的测试中，咖啡店老板娘娜洛曾给玩家留下一个颇有意思的印象：她不仅能接住当下的话题，还会记得此前聊过的事情。 哪怕隔了一段时间重新见面，她也不一定把玩家当成第一次光顾的陌生人。 甚至还有不少玩家在社交平台上，亲切地喊娜洛“妈妈”。 来自小红书《星布谷地》官方评论区 此前，《星布谷地》官方曾让咖啡馆老板娘娜洛接管小红书账号，与玩家进行互动。这种尝试在AI圈中并不稀奇，运营扮演角色也并不稀奇；稀奇的是，这是米哈游第一次尝试，让一个角色“自己”走出游戏，和玩家交流。 娜洛的“离职信” 对玩家来说，这是角色一句自然的寒暄；对游戏公司来说，背后却是一套需要长期运行的记忆系统。它既要从海量对话中找出值得保存的信息，又要在下一次互动时及时想起来，还得知道哪些事情不能让其他NPC听见。 更现实的是，玩家越多、聊得越频繁，这套系统就越贵。 假设一款游戏拥有10万月活跃玩家，每人每月与NPC交谈1

  • 游戏资讯

    • 让游戏里的NPC记住你，到底要花多少钱？发布时间：19小时前  |  标签： 《星布谷地》AI NPC

    在《星布谷地》的测试中，咖啡店老板娘娜洛曾给玩家留下一个颇有意思的印象：她不仅能接住当下的话题，还会记得此前聊过的事情。

    哪怕隔了一段时间重新见面，她也不一定把玩家当成第一次光顾的陌生人。

    甚至还有不少玩家在社交平台上，亲切地喊娜洛“妈妈”。

    来自小红书《星布谷地》官方评论区

    此前，《星布谷地》官方曾让咖啡馆老板娘娜洛接管小红书账号，与玩家进行互动。这种尝试在AI圈中并不稀奇，运营扮演角色也并不稀奇；稀奇的是，这是米哈游第一次尝试，让一个角色“自己”走出游戏，和玩家交流。

    娜洛的“离职信”

    对玩家来说，这是角色一句自然的寒暄；对游戏公司来说，背后却是一套需要长期运行的记忆系统。它既要从海量对话中找出值得保存的信息，又要在下一次互动时及时想起来，还得知道哪些事情不能让其他NPC听见。

    更现实的是，玩家越多、聊得越频繁，这套系统就越贵。

    假设一款游戏拥有10万月活跃玩家，每人每月与NPC交谈100轮，让NPC持续“记住”他们，到底要花多少钱？

    我们从现有游戏的实践、商业工具的报价，以及大模型的公开API价格入手，算一笔可以复核的账。

    NPC为什么需要记忆？

    过去，游戏中的NPC大多依赖预先写好的台词、条件触发和有限状态机。

    这样的设计并不落后，它足够稳定，也能承载出色的角色塑造。

    例如，《巫师3：狂猎》通过大量支线任务和分支选择，让玩家感受到NPC拥有自己的生活轨迹；《底特律：变人》则利用复杂的分支树，让角色关系随着玩家选择不断变化；《心跳文学部》等作品甚至证明，即使角色行为高度受控，只要文本和演出足够优秀，也能让玩家相信角色拥有独立人格。

    这些游戏依靠固定事件、好感度成长和阶段式对话，让玩家在重复互动中建立陪伴感。游戏中的角色并没有真正理解玩家，也不会记住玩家在现实中的经历，但通过精心安排的反馈循环，依然创造了一种“角色正在与你建立关系”的体验。

    但这类NPC也存在天然限制当玩家说出剧本之外的话，或者尝试探索未被预设的关系时，角色便容易暴露出背后的规则。：角色的“记忆”通常只存在于开发者提前设计好的变量之中。

    大语言模型解决了“能聊什么”的问题，却没有自动解决“我们聊过什么”。

    如果系统没有跨会话保存和读取记忆，NPC上一回还在安慰玩家，下一回登录就可能重新自我介绍。对于把陪伴作为核心体验的游戏而言，这种断裂尤其明显。

    《妹居物语》则是把长期记忆写进了产品卖点。根据Steam商店介绍，Yuki可以从交流中提取玩家的喜好、习惯和重要信息，角色性格也会随互动逐步发生变化。《不问凡尘》则把AI对话放进修仙世界：开发组展示过，NPC会根据与玩家的亲密度、过往经历改变说话方式，玩家的善恶行为也会影响后续关系与事件。

    这些游戏虽然侧重点有所不同，面对的却是同一道难题：记忆不能只停留在聊天框里，还得让玩家看见它如何影响人物关系和游戏世界。

    把NPC变成“有记性的人”，并不是靠保存全部聊天记录

    从表面上看，让NPC接入大语言模型并不复杂，但要怎么让NPC真正意义上记住玩家，恐怕才是需要真正苦心研究的。

    大部分人最容易想到的办法，是把玩家与NPC说过的话全部保存下来，下次对话时再一股脑交给大模型。

    但这样做并不划算。

    对话越长，输入Token越多；即使模型支持很长的上下文，也不代表它能稳定从数万字里找回最关键的一句话。

    更实用的做法，是把记忆拆分处理：近期几轮对话保留原文，维持眼前的交流；较早的交互抽取为事件、偏好、关系变化等摘要；需要回忆时，再根据当前话题检索相关片段，把少量有用信息交给模型。

    听起来有点像让大语言模型学会写日记和短讯，实际上，也正是如此。

    例如，玩家告诉角色自己不喜欢下雨，这可能是一条长期偏好；玩家昨晚在城镇里救过一个人，则是有时间和地点的事件；至于“早上好”“今天天气不错”，未必值得永久保存。

    系统需要判断信息的重要程度、可靠性与有效期，而不是见一句存一句。

    《代号：云端》制作人在今年5月的采访中谈到，其团队自研了一套名为Mnemo的拟人化长期记忆系统。按项目组的理解，角色不应机械地记住所有内容：玩家自己早已忘记的小事，如果NPC反复提起，反而显得奇怪；玩家格外重视的事情被迅速遗忘，同样会破坏陪伴感。

    团队希望在记忆准确率、回复延迟和成本之间取得平衡。制作人还表示，他们在研究常见Agent产品时发现，超过90%的Token可能被低效使用——这是该团队的工程观察，而非所有AI游戏都适用的行业统计。

    单个NPC的记忆尚且如此，当游戏里同时存在多个会交流的角色，问题还会更复杂。

    假设玩家只向NPC A透露了一个秘密，从未接触此事的NPC B却突然说破，即便语言生成得再自然，也会立刻露出破绽。

    因此，系统不只要记录“发生了什么”，还得记录“谁知道这件事、从哪里知道的、能不能继续传播”。

    公开活动、街头传闻和私人谈话，应当拥有不同的信息传播规则。

    米哈游在2026年云栖大会上介绍《星布谷地》时，就把这件事纳入了NPC系统的设计。其AI总负责人李嫣然提到，游戏角色使用统一的Agent架构，并搭载“超智记忆系统”，让部分事件能够在角色之间通过社交传播。

    街市发生的事情，可能成为咖啡馆里的谈资；与此同时，角色仍需维持各自的人设和认知范围。

    对这类生活模拟游戏而言，记忆不只是数据库功能，也是塑造世界真实感的手段。

    10万玩家和NPC聊天，游戏公司每个月要烧多少钱？

    如果只是验证AI NPC的玩法，开发团队可以直接购买现成服务。

    以AI NPC服务商Convai为例，其Indie Dev套餐售价29美元/月，包含3000次交互；Professional套餐售价99美元/月，提供1万次交互；Scale套餐则进一步提升到499美元/月，支持5万次交互和更高并发。

    这类服务已经将角色驱动、对话生成以及部分记忆管理能力封装其中，对于原型开发和小规模项目来说，可以快速验证玩法，而不必一开始就投入大量工程成本搭建完整系统。

    但在一款手游的正式运营阶段，固定套餐往往难以覆盖大规模需求。

    拥有技术能力的团队往往会选择调用大模型API，自行搭建记忆存储、检索和整理系统，以换取更高的控制能力。

    那么，一款拥有10万月活玩家的游戏，如果让NPC持续记住玩家，需要承担多少成本？

    为了让账单有可比性，我们先假设一个情形：

    这里没有包含数据库托管、服务器、运维、安全审核、网络和人工成本，也没有计算实时生成语音的价格。

    如果算上语音，那么这个价格则是的。突然倍增

    在这个设定下，10 万名月活玩家每个月产生1000万轮对话，模型推理和记忆处理成本约为 6908 美元。

    每轮NPC对话成本为：

    如果换成豆包，那么价格还能再低，例如豆包Seed 2.0 Mini在同样假设下，约为每月6000元人民币。

    更值得注意的是，随着玩家规模扩大，AI NPC的成本会呈近似线性增长。10万玩家能够承受的费用，放大到百万级用户后，会迅速成为一笔不可忽视的庞大长期支出。

    而如果说哪家模型最便宜——我去翻了翻现在国产主流模型的报价，大概是这么一笔数字：

    《谁最便宜》

    这里必须强调：这些数字是“给定Token用量×公开单价”的模型调用估算，不是上述游戏的实际运营账单，更不是完整的AI NPC成本。

    如果NPC还需要听懂玩家说话、实时配音，语音识别和语音合成又是另一笔费用。

    而且，1500 Token的平均输入只是一个经过压缩的示例，并非所有游戏都能做到。

    如果玩家聊得更久、单轮需要检索更多往事，或者跨不同模型使用，调用量会随之增加。

    反过来，缓存命中、批处理、减少无意义的模型调用，以及把简单反馈交给传统规则，都可能降低支出。

    而这，又将使我们回到游戏叙事设计最初的问题：

    角色的人格塑造，究竟依赖于什么？

    是依赖于无限的信息，还是恰到好处的反馈？

    算力省下了，成本未必消失

    除了选用不同的大模型，推理运行在哪里，也会改变游戏厂商的成本结构。

    云端调用最容易扩展，便于跨设备同步记忆，也不用要求玩家拥有高性能显卡。但玩家每多说一句话，就可能产生新的服务费用；遇到大量玩家同时上线，还要处理并发、响应速度与服务稳定性。

    另一种思路，是让玩家自己的设备承担部分工作。

    NVIDIA ACE与KRAFTON合作的《inZOI》提供了一个现成案例：Smart Zoi能够依据人物目标和经历安排日常行动、生成内心活动。

    NVIDIA曾披露，最初为其提供支持的是约5亿参数的Mistral-NeMo-Minitron小语言模型，在玩家本地设备上运行。

    这样不必为每次本地推理支付云端API费用，但模型部署、硬件适配与性能占用由开发团队和玩家共同承担。

    类似的思路在游戏图形领域已有应用，如DLSS利用AI模型进行图像重建，提高画面输出效率；而NPC智能行为则需要面对另一类模型部署问题。

    对于本身就有较高画面负载的游戏，GPU除了渲染，还要处理模型运算。模型越大、并发角色越多，对内存、显存和帧率的影响越需要实测。

    《INZOI》现在简中区仍是差评，大部分差评围绕着闪退，BUG等问题指出，还有更多玩家反馈玩不了。

    这些问题并不完全来自AI能力本身，但也说明AI想要真正进入大型游戏生产环境，除了模型效果，还需要面对性能、稳定性和工程适配等挑战。

    总的来说，AI在玩家端侧的部署应用，还有很长的路要走。

    结语

    AI NPC的记忆之所以有价值，未必是因为它能把全部聊天记录背下来。

    早在上世纪60年代，计算机程序 ELIZA 就展现了一个经典现象：即使机器只是依照简单规则回应，人类仍可能将理解、情感乃至人格投射到机器身上。

    如今，大模型的表达更自然，玩家当然更容易期待角色像人一样回应自己。

    但“像人”并不等于“事无巨遗”。

    NPC只需在玩家走进咖啡馆时，给予更特定的寒暄；或者因为共同经历过一件事，改变对玩家的称呼、态度或日常行为，而不是什么都要主动提起，例如玩家曾经随口说过的小事，或者已经不符合当前关系阶段的信息。

    否则，即使记忆准确，也会显得突兀。

    记忆只有在恰当的场景里发挥作用，玩家才会感受到关系正在延续。

    对于游戏公司来说，这恰恰构成了最难的取舍：存下多少信息、多久整理一次、哪些内容可以忘记、何时值得再把它取出来——以及，如何在体验、成本与用户隐私之间取得平衡。

    AI NPC的商业化问题，或许不只是如何以更低的成本储存和调用记忆，更在于如何将有限的技术资源转化为有价值的游戏体验。

    毕竟，让NPC记住玩家是一项技术能力，而让玩家相信自己被记住了，才是游戏设计真正需要解决的问题。

    元宇宙数字产业服务平台

    这些游戏依靠固定事件、好感度成长和阶段式对话，让玩家在重复互动中建立陪伴感。游戏中的角色并没有真正理解玩家，也不会记住玩家在现实中的经历，但通过精心安排的反馈循环，依然创造了一种“角色正在与你建立关系”的体验。

    但这类NPC也存在天然限制当玩家说出剧本之外的话，或者尝试探索未被预设的关系时，角色便容易暴露出背后的规则。：角色的“记忆”通常只存在于开发者提前设计好的变量之中。

    大语言模型解决了“能聊什么”的问题，却没有自动解决“我们聊过什么”。

    如果系统没有跨会话保存和读取记忆，NPC上一回还在安慰玩家，下一回登录就可能重新自我介绍。对于把陪伴作为核心体验的游戏而言，这种断裂尤其明显。

    《妹居物语》则是把长期记忆写进了产品卖点。根据Steam商店介绍，Yuki可以从交流中提取玩家的喜好、习惯和重要信息，角色性格也会随互动逐步发生变化。《不问凡尘》则把AI对话放进修仙世界：开发组展示过，NPC会根据与玩家的亲密度、过往经历改变说话方式，玩家的善恶行为也会影响后续关系与事件。

    这些游戏虽然侧重点有所不同，面对的却是同一道难题：记忆不能只停留在聊天框里，还得让玩家看见它如何影响人物关系和游戏世界。

    把NPC变成“有记性的人”，并不是靠保存全部聊天记录

    从表面上看，让NPC接入大语言模型并不复杂，但要怎么让NPC真正意义上记住玩家，恐怕才是需要真正苦心研究的。

    大部分人最容易想到的办法，是把玩家与NPC说过的话全部保存下来，下次对话时再一股脑交给大模型。

    但这样做并不划算。

    对话越长，输入Token越多；即使模型支持很长的上下文，也不代表它能稳定从数万字里找回最关键的一句话。

    更实用的做法，是把记忆拆分处理：近期几轮对话保留原文，维持眼前的交流；较早的交互抽取为事件、偏好、关系变化等摘要；需要回忆时，再根据当前话题检索相关片段，把少量有用信息交给模型。

    听起来有点像让大语言模型学会写日记和短讯，实际上，也正是如此。

    例如，玩家告诉角色自己不喜欢下雨，这可能是一条长期偏好；玩家昨晚在城镇里救过一个人，则是有时间和地点的事件；至于“早上好”“今天天气不错”，未必值得永久保存。

    系统需要判断信息的重要程度、可靠性与有效期，而不是见一句存一句。

    《代号：云端》制作人在今年5月的采访中谈到，其团队自研了一套名为Mnemo的拟人化长期记忆系统。按项目组的理解，角色不应机械地记住所有内容：玩家自己早已忘记的小事，如果NPC反复提起，反而显得奇怪；玩家格外重视的事情被迅速遗忘，同样会破坏陪伴感。

    团队希望在记忆准确率、回复延迟和成本之间取得平衡。制作人还表示，他们在研究常见Agent产品时发现，超过90%的Token可能被低效使用——这是该团队的工程观察，而非所有AI游戏都适用的行业统计。

    单个NPC的记忆尚且如此，当游戏里同时存在多个会交流的角色，问题还会更复杂。

    假设玩家只向NPC A透露了一个秘密，从未接触此事的NPC B却突然说破，即便语言生成得再自然，也会立刻露出破绽。

    因此，系统不只要记录“发生了什么”，还得记录“谁知道这件事、从哪里知道的、能不能继续传播”。

    公开活动、街头传闻和私人谈话，应当拥有不同的信息传播规则。

    米哈游在2026年云栖大会上介绍《星布谷地》时，就把这件事纳入了NPC系统的设计。其AI总负责人李嫣然提到，游戏角色使用统一的Agent架构，并搭载“超智记忆系统”，让部分事件能够在角色之间通过社交传播。

    街市发生的事情，可能成为咖啡馆里的谈资；与此同时，角色仍需维持各自的人设和认知范围。

    对这类生活模拟游戏而言，记忆不只是数据库功能，也是塑造世界真实感的手段。

    10万玩家和NPC聊天，游戏公司每个月要烧多少钱？

    如果只是验证AI NPC的玩法，开发团队可以直接购买现成服务。

    以AI NPC服务商Convai为例，其Indie Dev套餐售价29美元/月，包含3000次交互；Professional套餐售价99美元/月，提供1万次交互；Scale套餐则进一步提升到499美元/月，支持5万次交互和更高并发。

    这类服务已经将角色驱动、对话生成以及部分记忆管理能力封装其中，对于原型开发和小规模项目来说，可以快速验证玩法，而不必一开始就投入大量工程成本搭建完整系统。

    但在一款手游的正式运营阶段，固定套餐往往难以覆盖大规模需求。

    拥有技术能力的团队往往会选择调用大模型API，自行搭建记忆存储、检索和整理系统，以换取更高的控制能力。

    那么，一款拥有10万月活玩家的游戏，如果让NPC持续记住玩家，需要承担多少成本？

    为了让账单有可比性，我们先假设一个情形：

    这里没有包含数据库托管、服务器、运维、安全审核、网络和人工成本，也没有计算实时生成语音的价格。

    如果算上语音，那么这个价格则是的。突然倍增

    在这个设定下，10 万名月活玩家每个月产生1000万轮对话，模型推理和记忆处理成本约为 6908 美元。

    每轮NPC对话成本为：

    如果换成豆包，那么价格还能再低，例如豆包Seed 2.0 Mini在同样假设下，约为每月6000元人民币。

    更值得注意的是，随着玩家规模扩大，AI NPC的成本会呈近似线性增长。10万玩家能够承受的费用，放大到百万级用户后，会迅速成为一笔不可忽视的庞大长期支出。

    而如果说哪家模型最便宜——我去翻了翻现在国产主流模型的报价，大概是这么一笔数字：

    《谁最便宜》

    这里必须强调：这些数字是“给定Token用量×公开单价”的模型调用估算，不是上述游戏的实际运营账单，更不是完整的AI NPC成本。

    如果NPC还需要听懂玩家说话、实时配音，语音识别和语音合成又是另一笔费用。

    而且，1500 Token的平均输入只是一个经过压缩的示例，并非所有游戏都能做到。

    如果玩家聊得更久、单轮需要检索更多往事，或者跨不同模型使用，调用量会随之增加。

    反过来，缓存命中、批处理、减少无意义的模型调用，以及把简单反馈交给传统规则，都可能降低支出。

    而这，又将使我们回到游戏叙事设计最初的问题：

    角色的人格塑造，究竟依赖于什么？

    是依赖于无限的信息，还是恰到好处的反馈？

    算力省下了，成本未必消失

    除了选用不同的大模型，推理运行在哪里，也会改变游戏厂商的成本结构。

    云端调用最容易扩展，便于跨设备同步记忆，也不用要求玩家拥有高性能显卡。但玩家每多说一句话，就可能产生新的服务费用；遇到大量玩家同时上线，还要处理并发、响应速度与服务稳定性。

    另一种思路，是让玩家自己的设备承担部分工作。

    NVIDIA ACE与KRAFTON合作的《inZOI》提供了一个现成案例：Smart Zoi能够依据人物目标和经历安排日常行动、生成内心活动。

    NVIDIA曾披露，最初为其提供支持的是约5亿参数的Mistral-NeMo-Minitron小语言模型，在玩家本地设备上运行。

    这样不必为每次本地推理支付云端API费用，但模型部署、硬件适配与性能占用由开发团队和玩家共同承担。

    类似的思路在游戏图形领域已有应用，如DLSS利用AI模型进行图像重建，提高画面输出效率；而NPC智能行为则需要面对另一类模型部署问题。

    对于本身就有较高画面负载的游戏，GPU除了渲染，还要处理模型运算。模型越大、并发角色越多，对内存、显存和帧率的影响越需要实测。

    《INZOI》现在简中区仍是差评，大部分差评围绕着闪退，BUG等问题指出，还有更多玩家反馈玩不了。

    这些问题并不完全来自AI能力本身，但也说明AI想要真正进入大型游戏生产环境，除了模型效果，还需要面对性能、稳定性和工程适配等挑战。

    总的来说，AI在玩家端侧的部署应用，还有很长的路要走。

    结语

    AI NPC的记忆之所以有价值，未必是因为它能把全部聊天记录背下来。

    早在上世纪60年代，计算机程序 ELIZA 就展现了一个经典现象：即使机器只是依照简单规则回应，人类仍可能将理解、情感乃至人格投射到机器身上。

    如今，大模型的表达更自然，玩家当然更容易期待角色像人一样回应自己。

    但“像人”并不等于“事无巨遗”。

    NPC只需在玩家走进咖啡馆时，给予更特定的寒暄；或者因为共同经历过一件事，改变对玩家的称呼、态度或日常行为，而不是什么都要主动提起，例如玩家曾经随口说过的小事，或者已经不符合当前关系阶段的信息。

    否则，即使记忆准确，也会显得突兀。

    记忆只有在恰当的场景里发挥作用，玩家才会感受到关系正在延续。

    对于游戏公司来说，这恰恰构成了最难的取舍：存下多少信息、多久整理一次、哪些内容可以忘记、何时值得再把它取出来——以及，如何在体验、成本与用户隐私之间取得平衡。

    AI NPC的商业化问题，或许不只是如何以更低的成本储存和调用记忆，更在于如何将有限的技术资源转化为有价值的游戏体验。

    毕竟，让NPC记住玩家是一项技术能力，而让玩家相信自己被记住了，才是游戏设计真正需要解决的问题。

Research pdftitle=ResStreamGS: Residual-Sensitive Dual-Stream Gaussian Splatting for Mobile Volumetric Video Streaming, pdfauthor=Haoran Liu, Di Wu, Wang Luo, Hengyuan Na, Miao Hu, and Guocong Quan \vgtcinsertpkg\hypersetup\teaserRepresentative full-scene volumetric video scenarios and our mobile playback.

Introduction

ResStreamGS: Residual-Sensitive Dual-Stream Gaussian Splatting for Mobile Volumetric Video Streaming

Haoran Liu Di Wu Wang Luo Hengyuan Na Miao Hu and Guocong Quan

Abstract

Real-time mobile volumetric video enables immersive free-viewpoint experiences, but delivering high-quality 3D content under constrained bandwidth and computation remains challenging. Recent 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) systems, such as V, enable efficient mobile streaming by encoding time-varying Gaussian attributes with commodity video codecs and hardware decoding. However, existing pipelines treat all Gaussians as frame-varying signals, which is poorly suited to full-scene content where large portions remain temporally stable. Our empirical study shows that frame-wise adaptation and video coding of all Gaussians cause quality degradation in complex full-scene content, particularly in temporally stable regions. To address this issue, we propose , a residual-sensitive dual-stream framework that processes Gaussians according to their temporal behavior. ResStreamGS identifies residual-sensitive primitives through lightweight probe adaptation and reuses stable Gaussians within each Group of Pictures (GOP). Stable Gaussians are transmitted once per GOP, while only residual-sensitive Gaussians remain in the frame-wise hardware-decodable video stream. Experiments on complex full-scene volumetric videos show that ResStreamGS improves post-codec PSNR by 7.51–8.35 dB over a controlled V-style all-Gaussians baseline, reduces amortized payload by up to 56.5%, and achieves 30.883 FPS on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 778G platform.3ResStreamGS3

Mobile volumetric video streaming, real-time rendering, 3D Gaussian Splatting.

keywords

Volumetric video enables users to freely explore dynamic 3D scenes from arbitrary viewpoints and supports immersive applications such as virtual reality, mixed reality, and remote telepresence. Bringing these experiences to commodity mobile devices remains challenging because a practical system must maintain high visual quality while reducing transmission, decoding, memory, and rendering costs. 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides a promising representation for this setting because its explicit point-based formulation supports high-quality reconstruction and efficient rasterization . To further reduce transmission and decoding costs, recent systems organize time-varying Gaussian attributes into 2D video-like representations and compress them more effectively with commodity hardware codecs such as H.264 and HEVC .[]16[, , ]412032

Existing Gaussian-video pipelines encode the complete Gaussian representation as a frame-varying signal. This design is effective for human-centric or foreground-dominant content, where many important primitives change together with the moving subject. Complex full-scene volumetric videos have a different temporal structure. Dynamic regions occupy only part of the scene, while large portions of the geometry and appearance remain persistent over time. Treating all Gaussians in such scenes as frame-varying signals may therefore introduce unnecessary processing and distortion.

To better understand this limitation, we conduct an empirical study by applying the same V-style H.264 Gaussian-video pipeline to both foreground-focused and complex full-scene content. As shown in fig:v3_quality_drop, Neu3D consistently exhibits a much steeper PSNR decline across increasing QP values than Actors-HQ; under the default setting, the drops are 11.7 dB and 3.4 dB, respectively. More importantly, the qualitative results in fig:qualitative_comparison show that the errors are not limited to rapidly moving regions. Scene structures that should remain largely stable can also become visibly corrupted. These results suggest that the all-Gaussians formulation is poorly matched to the temporal structure of complex full-scene content.3\cref\cref

These results further motivate us to examine why full-scene content suffers more degradation. Our analysis in Sec.  shows that the key issue lies in a mismatch between the temporal behavior of Gaussian primitives and the granularity at which they are processed. Existing pipelines repeatedly adapt and encode every primitive at the frame level, even though many primitives change little within a short frame group. As a result, stable primitives are exposed to optimization drift and codec distortion without providing benefits in temporal adaptability. This observation suggests that Gaussian primitives should not be uniformly processed at the same temporal granularity. Stable primitives can instead be reused across frames, while only primitives sensitive to temporal residuals need to remain in the frame-wise adaptation and video-coding path.3

Motivated by these findings, we propose , a residual-sensitive dual-stream framework for efficient full-scene volumetric video streaming. ResStreamGS first uses lightweight probe adaptation to identify primitives that are sensitive to temporal changes. It then selects the smallest residual-sensitive subset that preserves the reconstruction quality of the composed scene. The remaining primitives are treated as stable references and reuse their keyframe attributes within the Group of Pictures (GOP). This partition produces two synchronized streams with different temporal granularities. Stable Gaussians are transmitted once per GOP and cached on the mobile device, while residual-sensitive Gaussians remain in a compact frame-wise Gaussian-video stream that can be decoded with commodity video hardware. In this way, ResStreamGS retains the advantages of hardware video decoding while removing persistent scene state from repeated frame-wise processing.ResStreamGS

Experiments on full-scene volumetric videos demonstrate that this design substantially improves both reconstruction fidelity and streaming efficiency. Under the same Gaussian-video coding framework, ResStreamGS improves post-codec PSNR by 7.51–8.35 dB over the controlled V all-Gaussians baseline while reducing the amortized payload by up to 56.5%. Our mobile implementation achieves 30.883 FPS on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 778G mobile platform, showing that high-quality full-scene volumetric video can be played in real time on commodity mobile hardware.3

(1) We identify a temporal mismatch in Gaussian-video streaming, where primitives with different temporal behaviors are uniformly processed at the frame level. This motivates processing Gaussians according to their temporal sensitivity. (2) We propose ResStreamGS, a residual-sensitive dual-stream framework that separates stable Gaussians for GOP-level reuse from residual-sensitive Gaussians for frame-level adaptation, with quality-aware selection to preserve reconstruction quality. (3) ResStreamGS substantially improves post-codec reconstruction quality while reducing the amortized streaming payload by up to 56.5%, and consistently achieves 30.883 FPS on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 778G mobile platform for smooth real-time full-scene volumetric video playback in practical mobile deployment scenarios.Our Contributions:New Perspective.Novel Framework.Superior Performance.

1

1.1

Dynamic novel view synthesis (NVS) reconstructs time-varying 3D scenes from videos for novel-view rendering. Early methods extend NeRF with deformation fields, scene flow, or time conditioning to model dynamic content . Later explicit and factorized representations improve efficiency using voxel grids, multi-plane decompositions, or tensorized 4D structures , but still rely on costly volumetric sampling or neural decoding.[, , , , , ]30353426399[, , , , ]7401836

3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) instead adopts an explicit point-based representation with rasterization-oriented rendering . Dynamic 3DGS methods further model temporal changes through deformation fields, Gaussian tracking, frame-wise updates, or pose-dependent Gaussian maps . Although these methods achieve high reconstruction quality and rendering speed, their large per-frame storage and limited compatibility with commodity video codecs make direct deployment for mobile volumetric video streaming challenging .[]16[, , , , , , , ]4329251449505224[, , ]432924

1.2

Despite efficient rasterization, 3DGS introduces substantial storage overhead because each Gaussian stores geometry, opacity, and view-dependent appearance attributes . Existing compact 3DGS methods mainly reduce this cost through opacity- or contribution-aware pruning, vector quantization, entropy coding, codebook-based clustering, and context-adaptive prediction . These techniques show that Gaussian representations contain spatial and attribute redundancy and can be compressed without severely degrading rendering quality. However, they are designed for static scenes, where the representation is decoded once and reused across viewpoints. Dynamic Gaussian sequences further amplify the storage burden as geometry and appearance evolve over time. Recent methods therefore exploit temporal redundancy through keyframes, residual modeling, motion-aware updates, and memory-efficient 4D parameterizations . Streaming-oriented approaches employ adaptive layering and saliency-aware tiling to reduce transmission cost . Nevertheless, most methods optimize how the complete Gaussian sequence is compressed, without distinguishing primitives that remain stable over time. Our work instead separates stable Gaussians from residual-sensitive ones before dynamic encoding, avoiding repeated lossy compression of stable structures and reserving the dynamic stream for time-varying content.[]16[, , , , , ]1831336215[, , , ]1948346[, ]1110

1.3

Mobile volumetric video systems must jointly reduce network bandwidth, decoding overhead, and rendering cost on mobile devices. Early systems based on point clouds or meshes employ visibility-aware scheduling, adaptive transmission, view-dependent content selection, and edge-assisted processing to support interactive playback under constrained resources . Recent 3DGS systems extend these ideas by adapting transmitted content, quality, or bitrate according to network conditions and user viewpoints . SwinGS  further adopts a sliding-window design to limit memory consumption and support longer volumetric video sequences. Video-coded Gaussian streaming takes a complementary direction by exploiting commodity video hardware. V maps dynamic Gaussian attributes into 2D Gaussian videos, enabling H.264 compression, hardware decoding, and shader-based rendering on mobile devices. Vega  further improves full-scene mobile streaming through object-level selective computation and view-adaptive scheduling, while MobileGS and SEELE optimize client-side Gaussian processing and rasterization . Despite these advances, existing video-coded pipelines still treat all Gaussians as temporally varying signals and repeatedly pass them through frame-wise compression. This can unnecessarily expose stable background primitives to quantization noise and optimization-induced attribute drift. Our work instead isolates stable Gaussians before encoding, preserving them across frames while retaining compact dynamic streams for real-time mobile playback.[, , ]134712[, , , , , , ]45372711104438[]283[]41[]17[, ]551

2

3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)  represents a scene as a set of anisotropic Gaussian primitives . Each primitive is parameterized as[]16G={gi}i=1NG=\{g_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}

gi=(𝐩i,𝐪i,𝐬i,αi,𝐜i),g_{i}=\left(\mathbf{p}_{i},\mathbf{q}_{i},\mathbf{s}_{i},\alpha_{i},\mathbf{c}_{i}\right),(1)

with , , , , and describing its position, rotation, scale, opacity, and view-dependent color, respectively. The rotation and scale determine the spatial extent of a Gaussian through its covariance matrix. Under a viewing transformation , the covariance is projected onto the image plane as𝐩i\mathbf{p}_{i}𝐪i\mathbf{q}_{i}𝐬i\mathbf{s}_{i}αi\alpha_{i}𝐜i\mathbf{c}_{i}𝐖\mathbf{W}

𝚺i=𝐑i​𝐒i​𝐒iT​𝐑iT,𝚺i′=𝐉𝐖​𝚺i​𝐖T​𝐉T,\mathbf{\Sigma}_{i}=\mathbf{R}_{i}\mathbf{S}_{i}\mathbf{S}_{i}^{T}\mathbf{R}_{i}^{T},\qquad\mathbf{\Sigma}^{\prime}_{i}=\mathbf{J}\mathbf{W}\mathbf{\Sigma}_{i}\mathbf{W}^{T}\mathbf{J}^{T},(2)

in which and are the rotation and scaling matrices, is the Jacobian of the projective transformation, and gives the projected covariance. During rendering, the Gaussians overlapping a pixel are depth-sorted and accumulated through front-to-back alpha blending:𝐑i\mathbf{R}_{i}𝐒i\mathbf{S}_{i}𝐉\mathbf{J}𝚺i′\mathbf{\Sigma}^{\prime}_{i}

𝐂=∑i∈𝒩𝐜i​αi′​∏j=1i−1(1−αj′),\mathbf{C}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{N}}\mathbf{c}_{i}\alpha^{\prime}_{i}\prod_{j=1}^{i-1}(1-\alpha^{\prime}_{j}),(3)

where contains the ordered Gaussians contributing to the pixel and is the corresponding projected opacity. This explicit representation enables efficient rasterization while maintaining high-quality novel-view rendering. For dynamic scenes, a volumetric video can therefore be viewed as a temporal sequence of these Gaussian attributes, whose values evolve from frame to frame.𝒩\mathcal{N}αi′\alpha^{\prime}_{i}

Building on this explicit representation, V organizes dynamic 3DGS into frame groups for volumetric video streaming. The first frame of each group is reconstructed as a keyframe, and subsequent frames are optimized sequentially from the preceding Gaussian representation. Motion is first estimated for the Gaussian primitives, followed by fine-tuning of the remaining attributes to improve temporal consistency across frames. By maintaining a consistent set of primitives within each frame group, the attributes of the same Gaussian can be associated across consecutive frames rather than reconstructed independently at every time step. After training, the per-frame Gaussian attributes are packed into 2D attribute images for video coding. V applies Morton sorting before packing so that spatially neighboring Gaussians are placed at nearby image locations, improving the spatial coherence of the resulting attribute maps. The same ordering is retained across attribute images and consecutive frames, allowing corresponding pixel locations to represent the same Gaussian primitive over time. As a result, the evolution of Gaussian attributes is converted into temporally coherent image sequences that can be compressed using conventional video codecs such as H.264. On mobile devices, hardware video decoders recover the attribute maps for standard 3DGS rendering.3[]413

3

In this section, we investigate why existing all-Gaussians video coding is poorly suited to complex full-scene volumetric video. This leads to our first research question.

3.1

Existing Gaussian-video pipelines treat the complete Gaussian representation as a frame-varying signal, which is well suited to human-centric content where many important primitives change together with the moving subject. Full-scene sequences such as and , in contrast, contain localized dynamic regions together with large persistent backgrounds and room-scale structures . To examine whether the same coding paradigm remains effective under this different temporal structure, we apply the V-style H.264 pipeline to both foreground-focused Actors-HQ and full-scene Neu3D across different quantization settings. As shown in fig:v3_quality_drop, Neu3D exhibits substantially faster PSNR degradation as QP increases, whereas Actors-HQ remains comparatively stable. Under the default setting, the corresponding drops are 11.7 dB and 3.4 dB, respectively, making the degradation on full-scene content more than three times larger. This consistent gap indicates that all-Gaussians video coding is substantially less effective for complex full-scene content.Effectiveness Analysis.cook_spinachcoffee_martini[]233\cref

To understand where this degradation occurs, we further examine the reconstructed scenes after Gaussian-video coding. As shown in fig:qualitative_comparison, the errors are not limited to rapidly moving objects or regions with strong temporal changes. Scene structures that should remain largely stable can also become visibly corrupted. This suggests that the degradation cannot be explained only by the difficulty of representing dynamic content. Instead, the frame-wise pipeline may unnecessarily perturb scene content that could otherwise remain persistent.Error Analysis.\cref

All-Gaussians video coding is substantially less effective for complex full-scene content than for foreground-dominant content, with considerable degradation even in scene structures that should remain temporally stable.Finding of RQ1.

This finding raises our second research question.

3.2

To identify the source of this degradation, we analyze nominally stable regions in through successive stages of the reconstruction and coding pipeline. As shown in fig:intro_diagnostic(a), using the frozen Gaussians as the reference, frame-wise retraining alone introduces a 4.69 dB PSNR drop, while subsequent video coding causes another 1.74 dB drop, resulting in a total degradation of 6.43 dB. This decomposition shows that stable scene content is affected by both frame-wise optimization and lossy video coding rather than by codec distortion alone.Stage-Wise Analysis.cook_spinach\cref

The attribute-level analysis in fig:intro_diagnostic(b) further shows that frame-wise retraining perturbs multiple Gaussian attributes even for primitives whose underlying scene content changes little. These slightly changed attributes are then repeatedly quantized and reconstructed as temporal video signals, introducing additional distortion. This problem is particularly severe for full-scene content because a large portion of its Gaussians correspond to persistent geometry and appearance within a short GOP. Frame-wise processing provides little benefit for these primitives, yet the all-Gaussians pipeline still repeatedly adapts and encodes them. Importantly, temporal stability does not correspond directly to a semantic foreground-background partition: some spatially stationary primitives still require frame-dependent updates, while some primitives near dynamic regions remain sufficiently stable for reuse. The key distinction should therefore be whether each primitive is sensitive to temporal changes that affect reconstruction quality.Temporal Mismatch Analysis.\cref

The degradation arises from a mismatch between primitive-level temporal behavior and frame-level processing. Uniformly adapting and encoding all Gaussians unnecessarily exposes reusable stable primitives to both optimization drift and codec distortion during repeated frame-wise processing stages.Finding of RQ2.

Gaussian primitives should be processed according to their temporal sensitivity rather than uniformly at the frame level. Stable primitives can be represented once and reused within a GOP, while only residual-sensitive primitives need to remain in the frame-wise adaptation and video-coding path.Insight for ResStreamGS.

4

Motivated by the above insight, we propose , an end-to-end residual-sensitive dual-stream framework for efficient mobile 3DGS streaming, as illustrated in Fig. . ResStreamGS organizes Gaussians according to their temporal sensitivity into a group-level stable stream and a frame-level residual-sensitive stream. The framework consists of server-side dual-stream GOP processing and mobile-side composition and rendering.ResStreamGS4

On the server side, ResStreamGS initializes the Gaussian representation from the keyframe and performs lightweight GOP probing to profile multi-attribute residual sensitivity. It then ranks the primitives according to their sensitivity and applies quality-aware ratio selection to partition them into stable and residual-sensitive subsets. Stable Gaussians are retained at the GOP level and reused across its frames, while residual-sensitive Gaussians undergo frame-wise motion estimation and fine-tuning to capture temporal variations. After optimization, the two subsets are organized into different transmission forms: stable Gaussians are encoded as a stable packet transmitted once per GOP, whereas residual-sensitive Gaussians are arranged into a compact frame-wise Gaussian video compatible with hardware-supported codecs for efficient transmission.

On the mobile side, the stable packet is received once at the beginning of each GOP and cached in device memory for reuse across subsequent frames. In parallel, the residual-sensitive Gaussian video is decoded frame by frame using commodity hardware video decoding. For each frame, the decoded residual-sensitive Gaussians are combined with the cached stable Gaussians to reconstruct the complete Gaussian representation for the current scene state. Given the current user viewpoint, ResStreamGS further applies view-frustum culling to discard invisible primitives, followed by opacity-based pruning to remove Gaussians with negligible rendering contributions. The remaining Gaussians are then depth-sorted and rendered to produce the final view. In this way, the mobile client avoids repeatedly decoding and storing persistent scene content while retaining frame-wise updates for temporally sensitive regions.

A lightweight probe temporarily adapts the keyframe representation to this target using the calibrated training views of the probe target frame. However, existing pipeline

Research pdftitle=ResStreamGS: Residual-Sensitive Dual-Stream Gaussian Splatting for Mobile Volumetric Video Streaming, pdfauthor=Haoran Liu, Di Wu, Wang Luo, Hengyuan Na, Miao Hu, and Guocong Quan \vgtcinsertpkg\hypersetup\teaserRepresentative full-scene volumetric video scenarios and our mobile playback.

Introduction

ResStreamGS: Residual-Sensitive Dual-Stream Gaussian Splatting for Mobile Volumetric Video Streaming

Haoran Liu Di Wu Wang Luo Hengyuan Na Miao Hu and Guocong Quan

Abstract

Real-time mobile volumetric video enables immersive free-viewpoint experiences, but delivering high-quality 3D content under constrained bandwidth and computation remains challenging. Recent 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) systems, such as V, enable efficient mobile streaming by encoding time-varying Gaussian attributes with commodity video codecs and hardware decoding. However, existing pipelines treat all Gaussians as frame-varying signals, which is poorly suited to full-scene content where large portions remain temporally stable. Our empirical study shows that frame-wise adaptation and video coding of all Gaussians cause quality degradation in complex full-scene content, particularly in temporally stable regions. To address this issue, we propose , a residual-sensitive dual-stream framework that processes Gaussians according to their temporal behavior. ResStreamGS identifies residual-sensitive primitives through lightweight probe adaptation and reuses stable Gaussians within each Group of Pictures (GOP). Stable Gaussians are transmitted once per GOP, while only residual-sensitive Gaussians remain in the frame-wise hardware-decodable video stream. Experiments on complex full-scene volumetric videos show that ResStreamGS improves post-codec PSNR by 7.51–8.35 dB over a controlled V-style all-Gaussians baseline, reduces amortized payload by up to 56.5%, and achieves 30.883 FPS on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 778G platform.3ResStreamGS3

Mobile volumetric video streaming, real-time rendering, 3D Gaussian Splatting.

keywords

Volumetric video enables users to freely explore dynamic 3D scenes from arbitrary viewpoints and supports immersive applications such as virtual reality, mixed reality, and remote telepresence. Bringing these experiences to commodity mobile devices remains challenging because a practical system must maintain high visual quality while reducing transmission, decoding, memory, and rendering costs. 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides a promising representation for this setting because its explicit point-based formulation supports high-quality reconstruction and efficient rasterization . To further reduce transmission and decoding costs, recent systems organize time-varying Gaussian attributes into 2D video-like representations and compress them more effectively with commodity hardware codecs such as H.264 and HEVC .[]16[, , ]412032

Existing Gaussian-video pipelines encode the complete Gaussian representation as a frame-varying signal. This design is effective for human-centric or foreground-dominant content, where many important primitives change together with the moving subject. Complex full-scene volumetric videos have a different temporal structure. Dynamic regions occupy only part of the scene, while large portions of the geometry and appearance remain persistent over time. Treating all Gaussians in such scenes as frame-varying signals may therefore introduce unnecessary processing and distortion.

To better understand this limitation, we conduct an empirical study by applying the same V-style H.264 Gaussian-video pipeline to both foreground-focused and complex full-scene content. As shown in fig:v3_quality_drop, Neu3D consistently exhibits a much steeper PSNR decline across increasing QP values than Actors-HQ; under the default setting, the drops are 11.7 dB and 3.4 dB, respectively. More importantly, the qualitative results in fig:qualitative_comparison show that the errors are not limited to rapidly moving regions. Scene structures that should remain largely stable can also become visibly corrupted. These results suggest that the all-Gaussians formulation is poorly matched to the temporal structure of complex full-scene content.3\cref\cref

These results further motivate us to examine why full-scene content suffers more degradation. Our analysis in Sec.  shows that the key issue lies in a mismatch between the temporal behavior of Gaussian primitives and the granularity at which they are processed. Existing pipelines repeatedly adapt and encode every primitive at the frame level, even though many primitives change little within a short frame group. As a result, stable primitives are exposed to optimization drift and codec distortion without providing benefits in temporal adaptability. This observation suggests that Gaussian primitives should not be uniformly processed at the same temporal granularity. Stable primitives can instead be reused across frames, while only primitives sensitive to temporal residuals need to remain in the frame-wise adaptation and video-coding path.3

Motivated by these findings, we propose , a residual-sensitive dual-stream framework for efficient full-scene volumetric video streaming. ResStreamGS first uses lightweight probe adaptation to identify primitives that are sensitive to temporal changes. It then selects the smallest residual-sensitive subset that preserves the reconstruction quality of the composed scene. The remaining primitives are treated as stable references and reuse their keyframe attributes within the Group of Pictures (GOP). This partition produces two synchronized streams with different temporal granularities. Stable Gaussians are transmitted once per GOP and cached on the mobile device, while residual-sensitive Gaussians remain in a compact frame-wise Gaussian-video stream that can be decoded with commodity video hardware. In this way, ResStreamGS retains the advantages of hardware video decoding while removing persistent scene state from repeated frame-wise processing.ResStreamGS

Experiments on full-scene volumetric videos demonstrate that this design substantially improves both reconstruction fidelity and streaming efficiency. Under the same Gaussian-video coding framework, ResStreamGS improves post-codec PSNR by 7.51–8.35 dB over the controlled V all-Gaussians baseline while reducing the amortized payload by up to 56.5%. Our mobile implementation achieves 30.883 FPS on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 778G mobile platform, showing that high-quality full-scene volumetric video can be played in real time on commodity mobile hardware.3

(1) We identify a temporal mismatch in Gaussian-video streaming, where primitives with different temporal behaviors are uniformly processed at the frame level. This motivates processing Gaussians according to their temporal sensitivity. (2) We propose ResStreamGS, a residual-sensitive dual-stream framework that separates stable Gaussians for GOP-level reuse from residual-sensitive Gaussians for frame-level adaptation, with quality-aware selection to preserve reconstruction quality. (3) ResStreamGS substantially improves post-codec reconstruction quality while reducing the amortized streaming payload by up to 56.5%, and consistently achieves 30.883 FPS on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 778G mobile platform for smooth real-time full-scene volumetric video playback in practical mobile deployment scenarios.Our Contributions:New Perspective.Novel Framework.Superior Performance.

1

1.1

Dynamic novel view synthesis (NVS) reconstructs time-varying 3D scenes from videos for novel-view rendering. Early methods extend NeRF with deformation fields, scene flow, or time conditioning to model dynamic content . Later explicit and factorized representations improve efficiency using voxel grids, multi-plane decompositions, or tensorized 4D structures , but still rely on costly volumetric sampling or neural decoding.[, , , , , ]30353426399[, , , , ]7401836

3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) instead adopts an explicit point-based representation with rasterization-oriented rendering . Dynamic 3DGS methods further model temporal changes through deformation fields, Gaussian tracking, frame-wise updates, or pose-dependent Gaussian maps . Although these methods achieve high reconstruction quality and rendering speed, their large per-frame storage and limited compatibility with commodity video codecs make direct deployment for mobile volumetric video streaming challenging .[]16[, , , , , , , ]4329251449505224[, , ]432924

1.2

Despite efficient rasterization, 3DGS introduces substantial storage overhead because each Gaussian stores geometry, opacity, and view-dependent appearance attributes . Existing compact 3DGS methods mainly reduce this cost through opacity- or contribution-aware pruning, vector quantization, entropy coding, codebook-based clustering, and context-adaptive prediction . These techniques show that Gaussian representations contain spatial and attribute redundancy and can be compressed without severely degrading rendering quality. However, they are designed for static scenes, where the representation is decoded once and reused across viewpoints. Dynamic Gaussian sequences further amplify the storage burden as geometry and appearance evolve over time. Recent methods therefore exploit temporal redundancy through keyframes, residual modeling, motion-aware updates, and memory-efficient 4D parameterizations . Streaming-oriented approaches employ adaptive layering and saliency-aware tiling to reduce transmission cost . Nevertheless, most methods optimize how the complete Gaussian sequence is compressed, without distinguishing primitives that remain stable over time. Our work instead separates stable Gaussians from residual-sensitive ones before dynamic encoding, avoiding repeated lossy compression of stable structures and reserving the dynamic stream for time-varying content.[]16[, , , , , ]1831336215[, , , ]1948346[, ]1110

1.3

Mobile volumetric video systems must jointly reduce network bandwidth, decoding overhead, and rendering cost on mobile devices. Early systems based on point clouds or meshes employ visibility-aware scheduling, adaptive transmission, view-dependent content selection, and edge-assisted processing to support interactive playback under constrained resources . Recent 3DGS systems extend these ideas by adapting transmitted content, quality, or bitrate according to network conditions and user viewpoints . SwinGS  further adopts a sliding-window design to limit memory consumption and support longer volumetric video sequences. Video-coded Gaussian streaming takes a complementary direction by exploiting commodity video hardware. V maps dynamic Gaussian attributes into 2D Gaussian videos, enabling H.264 compression, hardware decoding, and shader-based rendering on mobile devices. Vega  further improves full-scene mobile streaming through object-level selective computation and view-adaptive scheduling, while MobileGS and SEELE optimize client-side Gaussian processing and rasterization . Despite these advances, existing video-coded pipelines still treat all Gaussians as temporally varying signals and repeatedly pass them through frame-wise compression. This can unnecessarily expose stable background primitives to quantization noise and optimization-induced attribute drift. Our work instead isolates stable Gaussians before encoding, preserving them across frames while retaining compact dynamic streams for real-time mobile playback.[, , ]134712[, , , , , , ]45372711104438[]283[]41[]17[, ]551

2

3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)  represents a scene as a set of anisotropic Gaussian primitives . Each primitive is parameterized as[]16G={gi}i=1NG=\{g_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}

gi=(𝐩i,𝐪i,𝐬i,αi,𝐜i),g_{i}=\left(\mathbf{p}_{i},\mathbf{q}_{i},\mathbf{s}_{i},\alpha_{i},\mathbf{c}_{i}\right),(1)

with , , , , and describing its position, rotation, scale, opacity, and view-dependent color, respectively. The rotation and scale determine the spatial extent of a Gaussian through its covariance matrix. Under a viewing transformation , the covariance is projected onto the image plane as𝐩i\mathbf{p}_{i}𝐪i\mathbf{q}_{i}𝐬i\mathbf{s}_{i}αi\alpha_{i}𝐜i\mathbf{c}_{i}𝐖\mathbf{W}

𝚺i=𝐑i​𝐒i​𝐒iT​𝐑iT,𝚺i′=𝐉𝐖​𝚺i​𝐖T​𝐉T,\mathbf{\Sigma}_{i}=\mathbf{R}_{i}\mathbf{S}_{i}\mathbf{S}_{i}^{T}\mathbf{R}_{i}^{T},\qquad\mathbf{\Sigma}^{\prime}_{i}=\mathbf{J}\mathbf{W}\mathbf{\Sigma}_{i}\mathbf{W}^{T}\mathbf{J}^{T},(2)

in which and are the rotation and scaling matrices, is the Jacobian of the projective transformation, and gives the projected covariance. During rendering, the Gaussians overlapping a pixel are depth-sorted and accumulated through front-to-back alpha blending:𝐑i\mathbf{R}_{i}𝐒i\mathbf{S}_{i}𝐉\mathbf{J}𝚺i′\mathbf{\Sigma}^{\prime}_{i}

𝐂=∑i∈𝒩𝐜i​αi′​∏j=1i−1(1−αj′),\mathbf{C}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{N}}\mathbf{c}_{i}\alpha^{\prime}_{i}\prod_{j=1}^{i-1}(1-\alpha^{\prime}_{j}),(3)

where contains the ordered Gaussians contributing to the pixel and is the corresponding projected opacity. This explicit representation enables efficient rasterization while maintaining high-quality novel-view rendering. For dynamic scenes, a volumetric video can therefore be viewed as a temporal sequence of these Gaussian attributes, whose values evolve from frame to frame.𝒩\mathcal{N}αi′\alpha^{\prime}_{i}

Building on this explicit representation, V organizes dynamic 3DGS into frame groups for volumetric video streaming. The first frame of each group is reconstructed as a keyframe, and subsequent frames are optimized sequentially from the preceding Gaussian representation. Motion is first estimated for the Gaussian primitives, followed by fine-tuning of the remaining attributes to improve temporal consistency across frames. By maintaining a consistent set of primitives within each frame group, the attributes of the same Gaussian can be associated across consecutive frames rather than reconstructed independently at every time step. After training, the per-frame Gaussian attributes are packed into 2D attribute images for video coding. V applies Morton sorting before packing so that spatially neighboring Gaussians are placed at nearby image locations, improving the spatial coherence of the resulting attribute maps. The same ordering is retained across attribute images and consecutive frames, allowing corresponding pixel locations to represent the same Gaussian primitive over time. As a result, the evolution of Gaussian attributes is converted into temporally coherent image sequences that can be compressed using conventional video codecs such as H.264. On mobile devices, hardware video decoders recover the attribute maps for standard 3DGS rendering.3[]413

3

In this section, we investigate why existing all-Gaussians video coding is poorly suited to complex full-scene volumetric video. This leads to our first research question.

3.1

Existing Gaussian-video pipelines treat the complete Gaussian representation as a frame-varying signal, which is well suited to human-centric content where many important primitives change together with the moving subject. Full-scene sequences such as and , in contrast, contain localized dynamic regions together with large persistent backgrounds and room-scale structures . To examine whether the same coding paradigm remains effective under this different temporal structure, we apply the V-style H.264 pipeline to both foreground-focused Actors-HQ and full-scene Neu3D across different quantization settings. As shown in fig:v3_quality_drop, Neu3D exhibits substantially faster PSNR degradation as QP increases, whereas Actors-HQ remains comparatively stable. Under the default setting, the corresponding drops are 11.7 dB and 3.4 dB, respectively, making the degradation on full-scene content more than three times larger. This consistent gap indicates that all-Gaussians video coding is substantially less effective for complex full-scene content.Effectiveness Analysis.cook_spinachcoffee_martini[]233\cref

To understand where this degradation occurs, we further examine the reconstructed scenes after Gaussian-video coding. As shown in fig:qualitative_comparison, the errors are not limited to rapidly moving objects or regions with strong temporal changes. Scene structures that should remain largely stable can also become visibly corrupted. This suggests that the degradation cannot be explained only by the difficulty of representing dynamic content. Instead, the frame-wise pipeline may unnecessarily perturb scene content that could otherwise remain persistent.Error Analysis.\cref

All-Gaussians video coding is substantially less effective for complex full-scene content than for foreground-dominant content, with considerable degradation even in scene structures that should remain temporally stable.Finding of RQ1.

This finding raises our second research question.

3.2

To identify the source of this degradation, we analyze nominally stable regions in through successive stages of the reconstruction and coding pipeline. As shown in fig:intro_diagnostic(a), using the frozen Gaussians as the reference, frame-wise retraining alone introduces a 4.69 dB PSNR drop, while subsequent video coding causes another 1.74 dB drop, resulting in a total degradation of 6.43 dB. This decomposition shows that stable scene content is affected by both frame-wise optimization and lossy video coding rather than by codec distortion alone.Stage-Wise Analysis.cook_spinach\cref

The attribute-level analysis in fig:intro_diagnostic(b) further shows that frame-wise retraining perturbs multiple Gaussian attributes even for primitives whose underlying scene content changes little. These slightly changed attributes are then repeatedly quantized and reconstructed as temporal video signals, introducing additional distortion. This problem is particularly severe for full-scene content because a large portion of its Gaussians correspond to persistent geometry and appearance within a short GOP. Frame-wise processing provides little benefit for these primitives, yet the all-Gaussians pipeline still repeatedly adapts and encodes them. Importantly, temporal stability does not correspond directly to a semantic foreground-background partition: some spatially stationary primitives still require frame-dependent updates, while some primitives near dynamic regions remain sufficiently stable for reuse. The key distinction should therefore be whether each primitive is sensitive to temporal changes that affect reconstruction quality.Temporal Mismatch Analysis.\cref

The degradation arises from a mismatch between primitive-level temporal behavior and frame-level processing. Uniformly adapting and encoding all Gaussians unnecessarily exposes reusable stable primitives to both optimization drift and codec distortion during repeated frame-wise processing stages.Finding of RQ2.

Gaussian primitives should be processed according to their temporal sensitivity rather than uniformly at the frame level. Stable primitives can be represented once and reused within a GOP, while only residual-sensitive primitives need to remain in the frame-wise adaptation and video-coding path.Insight for ResStreamGS.

4

Motivated by the above insight, we propose , an end-to-end residual-sensitive dual-stream framework for efficient mobile 3DGS streaming, as illustrated in Fig. . ResStreamGS organizes Gaussians according to their temporal sensitivity into a group-level stable stream and a frame-level residual-sensitive stream. The framework consists of server-side dual-stream GOP processing and mobile-side composition and rendering.ResStreamGS4

On the server side, ResStreamGS initializes the Gaussian representation from the keyframe and performs lightweight GOP probing to profile multi-attribute residual sensitivity. It then ranks the primitives according to their sensitivity and applies quality-aware ratio selection to partition them into stable and residual-sensitive subsets. Stable Gaussians are retained at the GOP level and reused across its frames, while residual-sensitive Gaussians undergo frame-wise motion estimation and fine-tuning to capture temporal variations. After optimization, the two subsets are organized into different transmission forms: stable Gaussians are encoded as a stable packet transmitted once per GOP, whereas residual-sensitive Gaussians are arranged into a compact frame-wise Gaussian video compatible with hardware-supported codecs for efficient transmission.

On the mobile side, the stable packet is received once at the beginning of each GOP and cached in device memory for reuse across subsequent frames. In parallel, the residual-sensitive Gaussian video is decoded frame by frame using commodity hardware video decoding. For each frame, the decoded residual-sensitive Gaussians are combined with the cached stable Gaussians to reconstruct the complete Gaussian representation for the current scene state. Given the current user viewpoint, ResStreamGS further applies view-frustum culling to discard invisible primitives, followed by opacity-based pruning to remove Gaussians with negligible rendering contributions. The remaining Gaussians are then depth-sorted and rendered to produce the final view. In this way, the mobile client avoids repeatedly decoding and storing persistent scene content while retaining frame-wise updates for temporally sensitive regions.

4.1

For each frame group (GOP) , ResStreamGS takes the keyframe Gaussian set as its group-level reference. The keyframe establishes primitive correspondence and provides the initial values for all Gaussian attributes. The last frame of serves as the probe target. A lightweight probe temporarily adapts the keyframe representation to this target using the calibrated training views of the probe target frame. During adaptation, the probe records per-primitive attribute changes. These observations support residual-sensitivity ranking and the subsequent quality-aware selection of the residual-sensitive subset.ℱ={t0,…,t0+K−1}\mathcal{F}=\{t_{0},\ldots,t_{0}+K-1\}Gt0G_{t_{0}}ℱ\mathcal{F}

4.2

Position alone is insufficient to characterize residual sensitivity because other attributes may change a primitive’s projected contribution even when its center remains nearly fixed. We profile per-primitive changes over the attribute set , comprising position, quaternion rotation, scale, opacity, and DC color.𝒜={𝐩,𝐪,𝐬,α,𝐜}\mathcal{A}=\{\mathbf{p},\mathbf{q},\mathbf{s},\alpha,\mathbf{c}\}

Let denote the keyframe value of attribute for primitive , and let denote its value at a sampled state along the probe adaptation trajectory after burn-in. We use Euclidean distance for position, scale, and color, quaternion angular distance for rotation, and absolute difference for opacity. For each attribute, we compute the trajectory variance , where contains the sampled states after burn-in. These attribute-specific variances describe the instability observed while adapting the keyframe representation to the probe target.ai0a_{i}^{0}aaiiaiua_{i}^{u}uuvia=Varu∈𝒲⁡[da​(aiu,ai0)]v_{i}^{a}=\operatorname{Var}_{u\in\mathcal{W}}[d_{a}(a_{i}^{u},a_{i}^{0})]𝒲\mathcal{W}

Before aggregation, we normalize each attribute-specific statistic independently across the primitives in the frame group using

RNorma⁡(xia)=clip⁡(xia−median⁡(𝐱a)MAD⁡(𝐱a)+ϵ,0,zmax).\operatorname{RNorm}_{a}(x_{i}^{a})=\operatorname{clip}\left(\frac{x_{i}^{a}-\operatorname{median}(\mathbf{x}^{a})}{\operatorname{MAD}(\mathbf{x}^{a})+\epsilon},0,z_{\max}\right).(4)

Here, collects over all primitives in the frame group, denotes the median absolute deviation, is a small constant for numerical stability, and is the clipping threshold. The combined residual-sensitivity score is𝐱a\mathbf{x}^{a}xiax_{i}^{a}MAD\operatorname{MAD}ϵ\epsilonzmaxz_{\max}

ri=∑a∈𝒜wa​RNorma⁡(via),r_{i}=\sum_{a\in\mathcal{A}}w_{a}\,\operatorname{RNorm}_{a}(v_{i}^{a}),(5)

with equal attribute weights in the current implementation.

We rank primitives by the multi-attribute instability score obtained from probe adaptation. Lower scores indicate greater suitability for group-level reuse, whereas higher-scoring primitives are prioritized for frame-wise adaptation. The ranking is based on reconstruction-related attribute changes rather than semantic object labels, sensitive background structures may also receive high scores when their Gaussian attributes vary noticeably over time.rir_{i}

4.3

Given the sensitivity ranking, we construct nested candidate index sets. For a residual-sensitive ratio , referred to as the dynamic ratio in the experiments, the corresponding candidate index set isρ\rho

Sρ=Top⌈ρ​N⌉⁡({ri}i=1N).S_{\rho}=\operatorname{Top}_{\lceil\rho N\rceil}\left(\{r_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}\right).(6)

Here, is the number of Gaussians in the keyframe representation. All candidate index sets are derived from the same ranking, so whenever . Changing adjusts the number of selected primitives without changing the underlying ranking. The scores are ordered in descending order, so each Top- set retains the primitives with the highest residual-sensitivity scores.N=|Gt0|N=|G_{t_{0}}|Sρ1⊂Sρ2S_{\rho_{1}}\subset S_{\rho_{2}}ρ1<ρ2\rho_{1}<\rho_{2}ρ\rhoKK

For each candidate index set, primitives indexed by use their probe-adapted attributes at the probe target frame, while the remaining primitives retain their keyframe attributes. Both subsets are rendered together by the Gaussian renderer. We denote by the PSNR computed from the MSE pooled across the calibrated training views. The reference quality is obtained by assigning probe-adapted attributes to all primitives. Each candidate index set is therefore evaluated on the complete composed scene.SρS_{\rho}Q^​(Sρ)\widehat{Q}(S_{\rho})Q^full\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{full}}

We select the smallest candidate ratio whose composed-scene quality remains within an allowed degradation from the full-probe reference:δ\delta

ρ∗=min⁡{ρ∈Ω|Q^​(Sρ)≥Q^full−δ},\rho^{*}=\min\left\{\rho\in\Omega\;\middle|\;\widehat{Q}(S_{\rho})\geq\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{full}}-\delta\right\},(7)

where is the finite set of candidate ratios evaluated by the search and is the permitted probe-quality degradation. If no candidate satisfies the constraint, the largest ratio in is used.Ω\Omegaδ\deltaΩ\Omega

This rule directly minimizes the scope of frame-wise adaptation among the candidate partitions that preserve the required probe quality. It does not use post-codec PSNR or the fixed-ratio sweep reported in the evaluation; codec-level payload is measured separately after compression rather than during selection.

The selected index set defines ; the remaining keyframe Gaussians form . This partition specifies which primitives reuse their keyframe attributes across the GOP and which retain frame-dependent attributes.Sρ∗S_{\rho^{*}}Gr={gi∣i∈Sρ∗}G^{r}=\{g_{i}\mid i\in S_{\rho^{*}}\}Gs=Gt0∖GrG^{s}=G_{t_{0}}\setminus G^{r}

4.4

The stable and residual-sensitive sets continue to form a single scene after partitioning. For frame , the rendered image ist∈ℱt\in\mathcal{F}

𝐈^t=Render⁡(sg⁡(Gs)∪Gtr),\widehat{\mathbf{I}}_{t}=\Render\left(\sg(G^{s})\cup G^{r}_{t}\right),(8)

where denotes the differentiable Gaussian renderer and denotes the stop-gradient operation. Stopping gradients through freezes its keyframe attributes without removing the stable primitives from joint rendering and compositing of the complete scene. Only the parameters of are optimized during this stage.Render\Rendersg⁡(⋅)\sg(\cdot)GsG^{s}GtrG^{r}_{t}

For each non-keyframe, a residual translation field updates the primitive centers relative to their preceding-frame positions. The translated state is then fine-tuned to adjust geometry and appearance attributes. The stable set remains fixed and participates in every composed-scene rendering throughout the optimization process.

The fine-tuning objective is

Ltrain​(t)=Lrec​(t)+λT​Ltemp​(t),L_{\mathrm{train}}(t)=L_{\mathrm{rec}}(t)+\lambda_{T}L_{\mathrm{temp}}(t),(9)

where is the standard weighted combination of the and D-SSIM reconstruction terms evaluated on the complete rendered image. The temporal term applies only to the residual-sensitive subset.LrecL_{\mathrm{rec}}ℓ1\ell_{1}

We regularize frame-to-frame changes in scale, rotation, and opacity over the residual-sensitive subset. For normalized quaternions, accounts for the equivalent representations and . The temporal term isdq​(𝐪,𝐪′)=min⁡(‖𝐪−𝐪′‖2,‖𝐪+𝐪′‖2)d_{q}(\mathbf{q},\mathbf{q}^{\prime})=\min(\|\mathbf{q}-\mathbf{q}^{\prime}\|_{2},\|\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{q}^{\prime}\|_{2})𝐪\mathbf{q}−𝐪-\mathbf{q}

Ltemp​(t)=\displaystyle L_{\mathrm{temp}}(t)={}‖𝐬tr−𝐬t−1r‖F2Nr​D𝐬+1Nr​D𝐪​∑i=1Nrdq2​(𝐪t,ir,𝐪t−1,ir)\displaystyle\frac{\|\mathbf{s}_{t}^{r}-\mathbf{s}_{t-1}^{r}\|_{F}^{2}}{N_{r}D_{\mathbf{s}}}+\frac{1}{N_{r}D_{\mathbf{q}}}\sum_{i=1}^{N_{r}}d_{q}^{2}(\mathbf{q}_{t,i}^{r},\mathbf{q}_{t-1,i}^{r})(10)+‖𝜶tr−𝜶t−1r‖F2Nr,\displaystyle+\frac{\|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_{t}^{r}-\boldsymbol{\alpha}_{t-1}^{r}\|_{F}^{2}}{N_{r}},

where is the number of residual-sensitive primitives and and are the dimensions of scale and rotation. Residual translation already models positional change. Color is supervised through the composed reconstruction loss of the full scene.NrN_{r}D𝐬D_{\mathbf{s}}D𝐪D_{\mathbf{q}}

Selective optimization keeps fixed within the GOP and produces frame-dependent attributes for . The following subsection describes how the two representations are encoded as a reusable stable packet and a residual-sensitive Gaussian video.GsG^{s}GtrG^{r}_{t}

4.5

After optimization, encodes the stable set once per GOP for reuse and represents the frame-dependent residual-sensitive sets as a compact Gaussian video stream.ResStreamGSGsG^{s}GtrG^{r}_{t}

The attributes of remain fixed throughout the frame group . The stable packet is therefore encoded and transmitted once when the group is loaded. It stores the Gaussian attributes required for rendering together with the primitive indices needed to preserve their slots in the composed Gaussian set. The primitives are spatially ordered and packed by attribute type before entropy coding; the ordering, precision, and codec settings are reported in Sec. . Entropy coding is lossless on the quantized byte stream, while attribute quantization remains relative to the original floating-point representation. Keeping these persistent attributes outside the video path avoids repeated lossy coding and amortizes their transmission over frames.Stable Gaussian Packet.GsG^{s}ℱ={t0,…,t0+K−1}\mathcal{F}=\{t_{0},\ldots,t_{0}+K-1\}𝐁s\mathbf{B}^{s}5.2KK

retains the Gaussian video interface of V but applies frame-wise H.264/AVC coding only to , while remains outside the video path and is supplied by the reusable stable packet. This preserves hardware-decoder compatibility while restricting lossy temporal coding to primitives that require frame-dependent updates.Residual-Sensitive Video Packaging.ResStreamGS3[]41GtrG^{r}_{t}GsG^{s}

Each GOP is represented by . The metadata records primitive assignments, attribute layouts, quantization ranges, and synchronization information. It maps cached stable primitives and decoded residual-sensitive primitives back to their corresponding slots in the frame-wise Gaussian representation. The client loads once per GOP and advances frame by frame, reconstructing both subsets as a single primitive-level Gaussian scene rather than independently rendered sub-scenes.𝒮ℱ=(𝐁s,𝐕t0:t0+K−1r,𝐌ℱ)\mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{F}}=(\mathbf{B}^{s},\mathbf{V}^{r}_{t_{0}:t_{0}+K-1},\mathbf{M}_{\mathcal{F}})𝐌ℱ\mathbf{M}_{\mathcal{F}}𝐁s\mathbf{B}^{s}𝐕r\mathbf{V}^{r}

4.6

At each GOP boundary, the client decompresses and reconstructs using the metadata defined in Sec. . The stable primitives are uploaded to a GPU-resident cache and reused throughout the group. For each frame, the platform hardware video decoder processes , from which the player reconstructs . Only the residual-sensitive attributes and their corresponding GPU buffers are refreshed between frames. The cached and decoded primitives are composed before rendering:𝐁s\mathbf{B}^{s}GsG^{s}𝐌ℱ\mathbf{M}_{\mathcal{F}}4.5𝐕r\mathbf{V}^{r}GtrG_{t}^{r}

Gt=Compose⁡(Gs,Gtr,𝐌ℱ),𝐈^t=Render⁡(Gt).G_{t}=\Compose\left(G^{s},G_{t}^{r};\mathbf{M}_{\mathcal{F}}\right),\qquad\widehat{\mathbf{I}}_{t}=\Render(G_{t}).(11)

Composition is performed at the primitive level, allowing the two subsets to share visibility evaluation, depth ordering, and opacity accumulation within the same rendering pipeline instead of being rendered separately and blended in image space. The resulting Gaussian set then undergoes view-frustum culling and opacity pruning before depth sorting and Gaussian rasterization.

Keeping resident removes invariant attributes from the frame-level decode and buffer-update path, avoiding repeated stable-packet decompression, attribute reconstruction, and GPU upload. This caching alone does not reduce the number of primitives in ; without renderer-side filtering, the complete composed set still enters visibility processing. View-frustum culling rejects primitives outside the current view, while opacity pruning removes low-contribution primitives. These operations reduce the active Gaussian set passed to sorting and rasterization. Stable caching therefore avoids repeated decoding and state updates, whereas renderer-side filtering reduces sorting and rasterization workloads.GsG^{s}GtG_{t}

5

5.1

We evaluate on six complex full-scene sequences from two multiview video datasets, including five from Neu3D  and one from MeetRoom . These sequences contain localized dynamic content together with substantial room-scale structures, matching the streaming setting considered in this work. Each sequence contains 300 consecutive frames and is divided into 20-frame GOPs.Datasets and Evaluation Protocol.ResStreamGS[]23[]22

For each Neu3D sequence, we reserve five calibrated camera views for held-out evaluation and use the remaining views for training. MeetRoom contains 11 calibrated views, of which 10 are used for training and one is reserved for held-out evaluation. Neu3D rendering is evaluated at resolution, while MeetRoom is evaluated at . The same frames, camera parameters, resolutions, GOP boundaries, training views, and held-out evaluation views are used for all locally evaluated methods. All rendering metrics are computed exclusively on held-out views across evaluated frames. Probe adaptation and quality-aware stream partitioning use only training views, and held-out views are not used for model optimization or stream-configuration selection. Neu3D results are averaged over all five evaluated sequences.1352×10141352\times 1014640×360640\times 360

item.title: VAST开源实时世界模型EdenLive！单消费级显卡、720P超24FPS
item.description:
来源：量子位（中文） 相关度：22.4 正文：5131 字 / 8 图

命中：世界模型

让人人都能自由创造并体验可交互世界

< img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400">

VAST开源实时世界模型EdenLive！单消费级显卡、720P超24FPS

听雨2026-10-1819:49:49 来源：量子位

让人人都能自由创造并体验可交互世界

听雨 发自 凹非寺量子位 | 公众号QbitAI

VAST的世界模型，今天有了新成果。

实时世界模型，正式发布并开源。EdenLive

据VAST介绍，EdenLive首次实现了在实时生成的前提下，同时完成任意参考输入、任意画风生成和长时连续运行。

具体来说，给它简化场景或参考视频，再配上目标首帧和提示词，就能沿着参考的布局与运动，持续生成写实、二次元等不同画风的精细画面。

参考来源可以不同，生成画风可以指定，而这些变化都能在实时生成过程中呈现。

在单张消费级显卡Nvidia RTX 5090上、720P条件下，5B模型的生成速度，还能持续生成分钟级画面。超过24FPS

据VAST介绍，从用户输入操作到对应画面出现，这套系统目前的端到端延迟为百毫秒级。

画面持续变化的同时，交互规则和世界状态由上游交互系统维护。系统接收玩家操作、更新状态，EdenLive再根据对应的参考画面，将这些变化实时呈现出来。

最近，AI在3D场景搭建与交互创作上的能力，变得越来越直观。

就是一个典型例子：它已经能够在Blender里搭建房屋，再将其转入Unreal Engine 5，形成可以进入、漫游的场景。GPT-6 Astra

当AI能够搭建场景、设计交互玩法，如何让这些内容获得精细且实时的视觉表现，也就成为接下来需要解决的问题。

在这样的背景下，一条技术路线逐渐成为行业共识：。由交互系统维护底层状态和运行规则，再由生成模型负责视觉渲染

而这套分工，VAST早在今年6月初就已经明确并对外发布成果。

当时公开的Project Eden研究预览，已将作为核心设计。「状态维护与视觉渲染解耦」

从时间上看，这一路线选择早于行业共识形成约3-4个月。

如今，EdenLive作为这条路线的阶段性成果发布，并开放模型权重和推理代码，同步公开技术报告与端到端Demo。

https://github.com/VAST-AI-Research/EdenLive代码：

https://vast-eden.ai/?p=edenlive项目主页：

https://assets.vast-eden.ai/assets/edenlive/EdenLive-tech-report.pdf技术报告：

https://huggingface.co/VAST-AI/EdenLive开放权重：

多种参考输入，不同画风实时生成

EdenLive的核心价值，在于为简化场景和交互内容提供高质量实时渲染，底层逻辑与状态则继续由上游交互系统维护。

它具体能做什么？我们先来欣赏一波Demo。

交互式游戏预览

首先是交互式游戏预览，2D、3D场景都可以接入。

现阶段，EdenLive更适合场景漫游、推箱子等交互相对低频的玩法，让创作者在操作游戏原型的同时，查看精细画面下的呈现效果。

【此处无法插入视频，遗憾……可到量子位公众号查看～】

比如岩浆闯关，角色用冷冻枪制造落脚点，再通过跳跃一路前进。

要让这样的游戏画面随着操作持续更新，生成速度首先得跟上。

据VAST公布的数据，在单张消费级显卡RTX 5090、720P条件下，EdenLive的5B模型生成速度，也就是每秒生成超过24帧画面。超过24FPS

另一个Demo——双人对打游戏，则能具体展示角色动作与血条、回合计时等游戏状态的配合。

除了画面更新速度，按下按键后多久能看到反馈，也直接影响交互体验。

据VAST介绍，EdenLive目前从用户输入到对应画面出现，端到端延迟为百毫秒级。

这套系统还支持分钟级连续生成，让场景漫游和连续操作有更长的展开空间。

场景与动画预览

除了游戏互动，EdenLive还可以用于场景与动画预览，在场景布局和运镜已经确定的基础上，更换不同的美术风格。

比如，让大家天天玩的「鹈鹕骑自行车」成真……

从未见过如此栩栩如生之鹈鹕啊。

生成画面不仅让羽毛和海边环境有了细致的质感，还模拟出了真实的光影。

用简单模型搭出的雪地行车场景，经EdenLive生成后，也呈现出了更写实的车身纹理、积雪和光影效果。

这些画面的生成，由三类输入共同控制：参考画面提供场景布局、镜头与运动，目标首帧设定整体外观和画风，提示词则补充风格与细节。

因此，同一套布局和运镜，可以用来生成不同美术风格的版本，供导演和概念设计师比较、选择。

视频重渲染与换⽪

已有视频也可以交给EdenLive重新渲染，实时替换角色形象、画面内容和整体风格。

比如，将蓝色背景前的真人转换成卡通角色，但人物姿态和服装配色仍与参考画面保持一致。

这类用法类似虚拟主播换形象，以真人的动作作为参考，生成另一种角色外观。

再比如，将实拍房屋转换成手绘动画风格。

房屋的大体布局得到保留，屋顶、墙面和窗框则用线条重新勾勒，色彩与光影也变得更加柔和。

具⾝数据增强

EdenLive还可以用于具身数据增强，将真实人类操作画面转成机器人视角，并对第一视角视频中的物体和外观进行修改。

比如这段视频中，人手拿着喷壶和抹布清洁台面。

经EdenLive生成后，双手被替换成机械手，抹布从橙色变成了黄色，但清洁动作仍然与原视频保持一致。

除了替换操作主体，第一视角视频中的物体、材质和颜色也可以调整。

比如把人手替换成金属机械手臂，推车扶手换成银色金属质感，但抓握和推行的动作与原视频保持一致。

这样，已有操作视频就能衍生出不同外观的版本，为具身研究扩展视频样本。

从简单的2D动画、3D场景，到实拍视频和第一视角操作画面，这些不同来源的素材，都可以作为EdenLive的参考输入。

用同一模型接收多种参考，沿着已有布局与运动改变视觉表现，再以实时、分钟级连续生成的方式输出画面，正是这组Demo共同展示的核心能力。

现阶段，EdenLive也仍存在一些需要改善的地方。

高频、激烈的交互对生成速度和动作呈现有更高要求；多个角色同时出现时的身份保持、小物体的精细控制，以及长时间生成中的视觉一致性，也有进一步提升的空间。

不过，VAST已经开放了不同规格的模型权重和推理代码，同时公开了技术报告和上述端到端Demo。

官方还将同步开源，一款「Prompt to Proxy Game」Skill。Game Prototype Turbo

用户可以通过它快速生成可直接游玩的游戏原型。游戏运行时，交互系统持续更新状态，并输出对应的简化参考画面；EdenLive再将这些画面实时渲染为精细的视觉内容，反馈给玩家，形成从游戏逻辑到实时视觉呈现的完整链路。

大家都可以去体验一下～

拆解EdenLive技术路线与核心壁垒

接下来，我们来看看EdenLive背后的技术路线究竟是怎样的。

其采用的核心技术是，也就是把世界如何运行、画面如何呈现分开处理。「解耦世界状态与视觉渲染」

比如这段街头对打Demo：

角色的移动、攻击和防御，都由玩家按下相应按键来控制；交互系统接收操作，更新角色位置和动作，并判断攻击是否命中、血量如何变化。

EdenLive则根据这些变化生成画面，让左边简单的方块角色，在右边呈现为更写实的人物。

玩家看到画面反馈，再继续按键操作，游戏便沿着这套循环推进。

我们把这套分工放进完整管线，还能看得更直观：

图中，简化场景或参考视频提供布局与运动，目标首帧和提示词指定外观与细节。

EdenLive结合这些输入，持续输出精细画面；游戏逻辑和状态更新，则由上游交互系统负责。

这也呈现出了EdenLive在Project Eden中的职责。

是VAST长期推进的世界模型研究项目，EdenLive则是其中聚焦实时生成式渲染的阶段性成果。Project Eden

管线看起来清楚，但实际做起来，还需要同时兼顾几件事：

画面足够精细、动作跟得上参考、生成速度满足交互需求，还能持续运行。

这就涉及数据如何采集和配对，以及3D、视频生成与系统工程之间如何协作。

首先是。数据积累

要让模型把简单的方块角色生成写实人物，同时与参考画面保持相应动作，就需要建立参考与生成画面之间的对应关系。

场景布局、镜头运动和物体位置，都需要在数据中得到对齐。

据VAST介绍，其数据管线覆盖2D、3D简化场景、引擎渲染和真实视频等多种来源的成对数据。

从素材采集、场景构建到数据配对，这些工作共同支撑了EdenLive对不同参考和场景的处理能力。

第二层积累，来自。跨领域的团队协作

EdenLive涉及3D、视频生成与系统工程：既要处理空间结构和运动约束，也要生成细致的视觉效果，还要让模型以足够快的速度持续运行。

而VAST的团队配置，也覆盖了这几个方向。

这些要求需要放在同一套系统里协调。画面质量提高后，推理速度能否跟上；外观发生变化时，角色动作能否继续贴合参考，都需要模型与工程团队共同解决。

第三层积累，则是。路线判断与持续研发

在此前公开的Project Eden研究预览中，VAST已经明确提出设计：「解耦」

将世界状态与视觉生成分离，让底层状态独立于摄像机视角持续存在，再由渲染模块将其呈现为画面。

围绕这一思路，VAST进一步给出了三层架构：持续演化的结构化状态、状态到观测的接口，以及生成式神经渲染，分别承担状态维护、观测转换和画面生成的职责。

这一路线选择比行业共识提前了约三四个月。这段时间，也构成了团队沿着既定方向继续积累数据、打磨模型与系统的研发窗口。

沿着3D这条路，走向可交互的世界

从这套分工来看，。EdenLive延续的仍然是VAST原有的路线

构建一个可交互的世界，需要角色、道具和场景资产，也需要明确物体的位置、尺度与空间关系。3D为这些内容提供了可组织、可操作的基础，并参与世界状态的表达。

视频生成则负责细致的视觉呈现，将已有的结构与运动转化为丰富的材质、光影和动态效果。

两者结合，才能让创作者一边调整场景和玩法，一边获得相应的画面。

这也解释了，VAST为什么会进一步走向世界模型研究。

原有3D模型的能力，除了生成资产，还可以参与构建世界模型所需的数据。

在Project Eden的研究介绍中，VAST提到，团队利用已有3D能力，从视频中提取深度、相机位姿和几何运动轨迹等结构信息；同时，利用游戏引擎获取相互对应的状态信息与渲染画面。

这些工作，将VAST此前在3D模型和数据管线上的积累，延伸到了世界模型需要解决的结构、状态与视觉对应问题上。

从创作流程看，这条路线也在逐步扩大用户能够完成的事情：生成角色和道具，搭建场景，加入交互规则，再为运行中的内容赋予不同的视觉表现。

这也对应着VAST提出的愿景：。让人人都能自由创造并体验可交互世界

Project Eden承担着这一长期探索，EdenLive则先推进其中的实时生成式渲染环节。

对于创作者，它也提供了一个更具体的入口：把已经能运行的场景和玩法接入模型，在实际操作中尝试画面效果，在此基础上继续修改自己的作品。

One More Thing

等等，先别划走。

如果你感兴趣的话，VAST也在为这些研究寻找新同事。

其推出的，全年开放招聘，面向全球青年算法与研究人才，聚焦3D生成基础模型、三维理解、智能体与世界模型。V·STAR顶尖人才计划

VAST强调开放、扁平的研究环境，鼓励年轻研究者提出新想法，好的技术思路可以快速立项、验证，即便是实习生，也有机会参与核心模型训练，深入模型研发与工程实践。

待遇也是真的香～

无论是全职还是实习生都有机会拿到比头部大厂更具竞争力的薪资，特别优秀者上不封顶，还有长期期权。

如果你也想拥有定义问题的自由，从零推动一个项目，亲历一家头部AI公司从1到100的爆发式成长，获得最宝贵的创业经验，可以试试这个投递通道：

简历发送至vstar.talent@vastai3d.com，邮件标题请注明：VSTAR – 姓名 – 毕业时间

让人人都能自由创造并体验可交互世界

VAST开源实时世界模型EdenLive！单消费级显卡、720P超24FPS

听雨2026-10-1819:49:49 来源：量子位

让人人都能自由创造并体验可交互世界

听雨 发自 凹非寺量子位 | 公众号QbitAI

VAST的世界模型，今天有了新成果。

实时世界模型，正式发布并开源。EdenLive

据VAST介绍，EdenLive首次实现了在实时生成的前提下，同时完成任意参考输入、任意画风生成和长时连续运行。

具体来说，给它简化场景或参考视频，再配上目标首帧和提示词，就能沿着参考的布局与运动，持续生成写实、二次元等不同画风的精细画面。

参考来源可以不同，生成画风可以指定，而这些变化都能在实时生成过程中呈现。

在单张消费级显卡Nvidia RTX 5090上、720P条件下，5B模型的生成速度，还能持续生成分钟级画面。超过24FPS

据VAST介绍，从用户输入操作到对应画面出现，这套系统目前的端到端延迟为百毫秒级。

画面持续变化的同时，交互规则和世界状态由上游交互系统维护。系统接收玩家操作、更新状态，EdenLive再根据对应的参考画面，将这些变化实时呈现出来。

最近，AI在3D场景搭建与交互创作上的能力，变得越来越直观。

就是一个典型例子：它已经能够在Blender里搭建房屋，再将其转入Unreal Engine 5，形成可以进入、漫游的场景。GPT-6 Astra

当AI能够搭建场景、设计交互玩法，如何让这些内容获得精细且实时的视觉表现，也就成为接下来需要解决的问题。

在这样的背景下，一条技术路线逐渐成为行业共识：。由交互系统维护底层状态和运行规则，再由生成模型负责视觉渲染

而这套分工，VAST早在今年6月初就已经明确并对外发布成果。

当时公开的Project Eden研究预览，已将作为核心设计。「状态维护与视觉渲染解耦」

从时间上看，这一路线选择早于行业共识形成约3-4个月。

如今，EdenLive作为这条路线的阶段性成果发布，并开放模型权重和推理代码，同步公开技术报告与端到端Demo。

https://github.com/VAST-AI-Research/EdenLive代码：

https://vast-eden.ai/?p=edenlive项目主页：

https://assets.vast-eden.ai/assets/edenlive/EdenLive-tech-report.pdf技术报告：

https://huggingface.co/VAST-AI/EdenLive开放权重：

多种参考输入，不同画风实时生成

EdenLive的核心价值，在于为简化场景和交互内容提供高质量实时渲染，底层逻辑与状态则继续由上游交互系统维护。

它具体能做什么？我们先来欣赏一波Demo。

交互式游戏预览

首先是交互式游戏预览，2D、3D场景都可以接入。

现阶段，EdenLive更适合场景漫游、推箱子等交互相对低频的玩法，让创作者在操作游戏原型的同时，查看精细画面下的呈现效果。

【此处无法插入视频，遗憾……可到量子位公众号查看～】

比如岩浆闯关，角色用冷冻枪制造落脚点，再通过跳跃一路前进。

要让这样的游戏画面随着操作持续更新，生成速度首先得跟上。

据VAST公布的数据，在单张消费级显卡RTX 5090、720P条件下，EdenLive的5B模型生成速度，也就是每秒生成超过24帧画面。超过24FPS

另一个Demo——双人对打游戏，则能具体展示角色动作与血条、回合计时等游戏状态的配合。

除了画面更新速度，按下按键后多久能看到反馈，也直接影响交互体验。

据VAST介绍，EdenLive目前从用户输入到对应画面出现，端到端延迟为百毫秒级。

这套系统还支持分钟级连续生成，让场景漫游和连续操作有更长的展开空间。

场景与动画预览

除了游戏互动，EdenLive还可以用于场景与动画预览，在场景布局和运镜已经确定的基础上，更换不同的美术风格。

比如，让大家天天玩的「鹈鹕骑自行车」成真……

从未见过如此栩栩如生之鹈鹕啊。

生成画面不仅让羽毛和海边环境有了细致的质感，还模拟出了真实的光影。

用简单模型搭出的雪地行车场景，经EdenLive生成后，也呈现出了更写实的车身纹理、积雪和光影效果。

这些画面的生成，由三类输入共同控制：参考画面提供场景布局、镜头与运动，目标首帧设定整体外观和画风，提示词则补充风格与细节。

因此，同一套布局和运镜，可以用来生成不同美术风格的版本，供导演和概念设计师比较、选择。

这样，已有操作视频就能衍生出不同外观的版本，为具身研究扩展视频样本。

从简单的2D动画、3D场景，到实拍视频和第一视角操作画面，这些不同来源的素材，都可以作为EdenLive的参考输入。

要让模型把简单的方块角色生成写实人物，同时与参考画面保持相应动作，就需要建立参考与生成画面之间的对应关系。

场景布局、镜头运动和物体位置，都需要在数据中得到对齐。

据VAST介绍，其数据管线覆盖2D、3D简化场景、引擎渲染和真实视频等多种来源的成对数据。

从素材采集、场景构建到数据配对，这些工作共同支撑了EdenLive对不同参考和场景的处理能力。

第二层积累，来自。跨领域的团队协作

EdenLive涉及3D、视频生成与系统工程：既要处理空间结构和运动约束，也要生成细致的视觉效果，还要让模型以足够快的速度持续运行。

而VAST的团队配置，也覆盖了这几个方向。

这些要求需要放在同一套系统里协调。画面质量提高后，推理速度能否跟上；外观发生变化时，角色动作能否继续贴合参考，都需要模型与工程团队共同解决。

第三层积累，则是。路线判断与持续研发

在此前公开的Project Eden研究预览中，VAST已经明确提出设计：「解耦」

将世界状态与视觉生成分离，让底层状态独立于摄像机视角持续存在，再由渲染模块将其呈现为画面。

围绕这一思路，VAST进一步给出了三层架构：持续演化的结构化状态、状态到观测的接口，以及生成式神经渲染，分别承担状态维护、观测转换和画面生成的职责。

这一路线选择比行业共识提前了约三四个月。这段时间，也构成了团队沿着既定方向继续积累数据、打磨模型与系统的研发窗口。

沿着3D这条路，走向可交互的世界

从这套分工来看，。EdenLive延续的仍然是VAST原有的路线

构建一个可交互的世界，需要角色、道具和场景资产，也需要明确物体的位置、尺度与空间关系。3D为这些内容提供了可组织、可操作的基础，并参与世界状态的表达。

视频生成则负责细致的视觉呈现，将已有的结构与运动转化为丰富的材质、光影和动态效果。

两者结合，才能让创作者一边调整场景和玩法，一边获得相应的画面。

这也解释了，VAST为什么会进一步走向世界模型研究。

原有3D模型的能力，除了生成资产，还可以参与构建世界模型所需的数据。

在Project Eden的研究介绍中，VAST提到，团队利用已有3D能力，从视频中提取深度、相机位姿和几何运动轨迹等结构信息；同时，利用游戏引擎获取相互对应的状态信息与渲染画面。

这些工作，将VAST此前在3D模型和数据管线上的积累，延伸到了世界模型需要解决的结构、状态与视觉对应问题上。

从创作流程看，这条路线也在逐步扩大用户能够完成的事情：生成角色和道具，搭建场景，加入交互规则，再为运行中的内容赋予不同的视觉表现。

这也对应着VAST提出的愿景：。让人人都能自由创造并体验可交互世界

Project Eden承担着这一长期探索，EdenLive则先推进其中的实时生成式渲染环节。

对于创作者，它也提供了一个更具体的入口：把已经能运行的场景和玩法接入模型，在实际操作中尝试画面效果，在此基础上继续修改自己的作品。

One More Thing

等等，先别划走。

如果你感兴趣的话，VAST也在为这些研究寻找新同事。

其推出的，全年开放招聘，面向全球青年算法与研究人才，聚焦3D生成基础模型、三维理解、智能体与世界模型。V·STAR顶尖人才计划

VAST强调开放、扁平的研究环境，鼓励年轻研究者提出新想法，好的技术思路可以快速立项、验证，即便是实习生，也有机会参与核心模型训练，深入模型研发与工程实践。

待遇也是真的香～

无论是全职还是实习生都有机会拿到比头部大厂更具竞争力的薪资，特别优秀者上不封顶，还有长期期权。

如果你也想拥有定义问题的自由，从零推动一个项目，亲历一家头部AI公司从1到100的爆发式成长，获得最宝贵的创业经验，可以试试这个投递通道：

item.title: The Double-Edged Sword of Open-Ended Interaction: How LLM-Driven NPCs Affect Players' Cognitive Load and Gaming Experience
item.description:
来源：arXiv·NPC/智能体（English） 相关度：21.0 正文：4167 字 / 3 图

命中：npc

This study examines how large language model-driven non-player characters (LLM-NPCs) affect players' cognitive load and gaming experience, with a particular focus on the underlying psychological mechanisms, differences across task scenarios, and the role of individual traits. Conducting a randomized between-subject experiment (N=130) in a self-developed game prototype "Campus Culture Week", we com

[Submitted on 11 Apr 2026 (), last revised 18 Oct 2026 (this version, v3)]v1

Title:

, , , , Authors:Ting-Chen HsuWenran ChenJiangxu LinFei QinZheyuan ZhangView PDF
This study examines how large language model-driven non-player characters (LLM-NPCs) affect players' cognitive load and gaming experience, with a particular focus on the underlying psychological mechanisms, differences across task scenarios, and the role of individual traits. Conducting a randomized between-subject experiment (N=130) in a self-developed game prototype "Campus Culture Week", we compared player interactions with LLM-NPCs and traditional pre-scripted NPCs across multiple interactive modules. The results showed that the LLM-NPC condition, which combined free-form natural-language input with LLM-generated responses, produced higher cognitive load than preset-option scripted NPC interaction (p < .001), with expressive effort and response uncertainty as significant mediating pathways. However, LLM-NPCs did not yield a statistically significant improvement in overall gaming experience (p = .195); while they positively influenced players' perceived autonomy, they exerted a negative influence on system usability and trust. The effects of LLM-NPCs also significantly varied across task scenarios (p < .001), with stronger increases in cognitive load in more open-ended modules such as content creation and relationship building. The influence of individual differences was generally limited, with no robust associations remaining after correction for multiple comparisons. This study provides empirical evidence for understanding the "double-edged sword" effect of LLM-NPCs on player experience, and highlights the importance of scenario-sensitive and user-sensitive design in intelligent NPC systems.
