item.title: MeshSuite: A Unified Benchmark for Triangle- and Mesh-Based Neural Rendering
item.description:
来源：arXiv·神经渲染（English） 相关度：18.9 正文：34930 字 / 0 图

命中：neural rendering、rendering、mesh、splatting、rasterization

Triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering seeks to bridge neural representations and graphics engines through triangle primitives compatible with standard rasterization. Yet existing methods were developed and evaluated under inconsistent settings, with few direct comparisons and little evaluation in graphics engines. We introduce MeshSuite, the first benchmark for systematic evaluation of engine

License: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 arXiv:2609.01306v4 [cs.GR] 16 Oct 2026

MeshSuite: A Unified Benchmark for Triangle- and Mesh-Based Neural Rendering

Kaixuan Zhang Nanjing University of Science and Technology Affiliation: Minxian Li †Corresponding author.†thanks: Nanjing University of Science and Technology Affiliation: Mingwu Ren Nanjing University of Science and Technology Affiliation: Xiatian Zhu University of Surrey Affiliation: 

Abstract

Triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering aims to bridge neural scene representations and existing graphics engines (, Unity, Blender) by leveraging primitives compatible with standard rasterization hardware. There have been several such methods driven by parallel efforts, developed and evaluated under inconsistent settings, with little or no comparison with each other; critically, most even have never used graphics engines for evaluation nor considered deployability in practice – significantly undermining the objective and motivation. To address these issues, we introduce , the first benchmark of its kind to enable systematic evaluation of graphics-engine deployment and the reference Source Renderer for triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering methods. Importantly, our deployment protocol includes two engine deployment settings: (1) – a conventional opaque mesh pipeline with vertex colors and hardware Z-buffering; (2) – adding method-specific engine implementations supporting the retained appearance and compositing features (, alpha blending), so that the characteristics of each specific model can be taken into account. For mesh splatting, we further propose a structural audit of exported surfaces, diagnosing topological and geometric integrity toward downstream graphics assets. We highlight several results: (1) Graphics engine deployment would incur image-quality degradation under both deployment options. Among the triangle- and mesh-based NVS methods studied, MeshSplatting degrades the least under Standard Mesh Deployment. (2) The deployment setting matters – Custom Engine Deployment can retain the majority of fidelity at a roughly 533 slowdown relative to Standard Mesh Deployment across the two deployment datasets. (3) About mesh splatting, the current approaches to explicit connectivity and shared indexing are still limited: shared vertex indexing alone does not ensure manifoldness or global connectivity. From this benchmark, we validate that , and highlight the significance of assessing the graphics engine deployment process (, the degree of engine compatibility). The project page is accessible at .e.g.triangleMeshSuiteStandard Mesh DeploymentCustom Engine Deploymente.g.∼\sim×\timesrasterizability is merely part of graphics readinesse.g.https://surrey-up-lab.github.io/MeshSuite

1

Reconstructing a scene from multi-view images allows users to explore it from arbitrary viewpoints beyond those originally captured, supporting a wide range of vision and graphics applications, including AR/VR , gaming , and robotic perception . Recent advances in neural rendering, particularly Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) , have enabled increasingly realistic novel-view synthesis (NVS). Specifically, NeRFs use multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) to encode scene density and view-dependent color, synthesizing novel views through volume rendering . However, their practical use is constrained by high computational costs and the lack of an explicit geometric representation. In contrast, 3DGS represents scenes explicitly with 3D Gaussian primitives and uses efficient differentiable splatting to substantially reduce rendering costs .()Broxton et al., 2020()Lachambre et al., 2017()Zhu et al., 2022()Mildenhall et al., 2020()Kerbl et al., 2023()Mildenhall et al., 2020()Kerbl et al., 2023

Despite these advances, neither representation is directly compatible with the standard rendering pipelines of established computer graphics (CG) engines, such as Blender and Unity . These engines have benefited from decades of development and optimization, providing efficient rendering pipelines and integrated tools for lighting and shadows, material editing, and animation. Their mature ecosystems also offer extensive collections of reusable assets and plugins , facilitating the integration of reconstructed scenes into practical applications.()Blender Foundation, 2026()Unity Technologies, 2026(; )Unity Technologies, 2026Blender Foundation, 2026

To better take advantage of these engines, researchers have increasingly explored triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering methods, which optimize triangle primitives already supported by standard graphics hardware . These methods have demonstrated impressive NVS performance comparable to that of NeRFs and 3DGS, while offering a promising path toward integration with existing CG engines . However, existing triangle- and mesh-based works follow separate evaluation protocols, with differences in data preprocessing, image formats, evaluation metrics, and metric implementations, and none evaluates the methods in a graphics engine. Using triangles alone also does not ensure complete engine compatibility. Existing methods use triangles with substantially different features (Tab. ), including continuous or discrete opacity , coverage defined inside or outside a triangle , varying color representations (, view-dependent spherical harmonics (SHs) or neural networks ), and the presence or absence of neural texture decoders . These variations pose challenges for engine rendering and may require method-specific shaders, buffers, sorting strategies, and runtime state. Furthermore, existing mesh splatting methods evaluate exported mesh quality solely through vertex sharing, lacking a comprehensive analysis of critical structural and topological properties such as manifoldness and global connectivity.(; )Held et al., 2026bHeld et al., 2026a(; ; )Held et al., 2026bSheng et al., 2025Held et al., 2026a1(; )Held et al., 2026bHeld et al., 2026a(; )Sheng et al., 2025Held et al., 2026be.g.()Held et al., 2026a()Tojo et al., 2026(; )Tojo et al., 2026Held et al., 2026b()Held et al., 2026a

To address these questions, we introduce , a unified benchmark for evaluating triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering (see Fig. ). This benchmark enables: (a) integration of existing triangle- and mesh-based splatting methods; (b) fair and consistent comparison of different methods in a unified setting; (c) extensive evaluation of both triangle- and mesh-based models during training and inference; (d) Source Renderer evaluation and two engine deployment settings: - converting a trained model to a standard opaque vertex-colored mesh before rendering in a graphics engine; - adding a customized layer to implement method-specific designs, such as specialized appearance representations and alpha compositing.MeshSuite1Standard Mesh DeploymentCustom Engine Deployment

We note three key findings. , engine deployment reduces visual quality relative to the Source Renderer, with MeshSplatting losing the least quality under Standard Mesh Deployment among the studied methods (Tab. ). Second, Custom Engine Deployment produces more visually appealing renderings than Standard Mesh Deployment, at the cost of a roughly 533 slowdown (Tab. ). Third, existing mesh splatting methods’ exported meshes exhibit non-manifold structures and substantial fragmentation (Tab. ). These results show that ; appearance preservation, efficiency, and mesh structure must be evaluated together.First()Held et al., 2026a4∼\sim×\times46using triangles alone does not ensure graphics readiness

Our are as follows: () the first unified benchmark, , for evaluating triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering methods; () Custom Engine Deployment of existing methods in a graphics engine (, Unity), retaining their specific designs during engine rendering; and () an extensive evaluation of existing models in terms of novel-view synthesis, training/inference cost, and mesh structure.contributionsIMeshSuiteIIi.e.III

2

Novel-view synthesis (NVS) aims to synthesize images of a scene from viewpoints beyond those observed in the input images. A central component of this task is a scene representation that captures both geometry and appearance. NeRF represents a scene as a continuous function and synthesize views through volumetric integration . Later methods improve reconstruction quality and anti-aliasing or accelerate rendering through explicit, factorized, and hashed structures . 3DGS replaces repeated network queries with optimized anisotropic Gaussian primitives and a dedicated splatting rasterizer . Follow-up works refine Gaussian optimization or encourages surface-aligned geometry . These methods establish strong NVS baselines, but their representations are not natively supported by conventional graphics engines (, Unity and Blender). Integration with existing CG engines therefore requires specialized rendering implementations or conversion to mesh-based assets.Dominant neural representations.()Mildenhall et al., 2020(; ; )Barron et al., 2021Barron et al., 2022Barron et al., 2023(; ; ; ; )Reiser et al., 2024Yu et al., 2021Fridovich-Keil et al., 2022Chen et al., 2022Müller et al., 2022()Kerbl et al., 2023(; ; )Kheradmand et al., 2024Huang et al., 2024Guédon and Lepetit, 2024e.g.

To facilitate integration with conventional graphics engines, methods such as MobileNeRF and BakedSDF convert learned radiance fields into mesh-based representations. For explicit splats, SuGaR and GaMeS extract mesh surfaces from 3D Gaussian primitives or bind Gaussian primitives to deformable mesh faces. Although these conversion pipelines produce standard mesh assets, they often rely on lossy post-processing (, Marching Cubes, Poisson surface reconstruction, or heuristic simplification) that decouples the optimization target from the final rendering objective.()Chen et al., 2023()Yariv et al., 2023()Guédon and Lepetit, 2024()Waczyńska et al., 2024e.g.

Established CG engines, such as Blender and Unity , provide optimized rendering pipelines and integrated tools for scene editing, lighting, and animation, together with mature ecosystems of reusable assets and plugins. Triangle meshes are widely supported by these pipelines, making them a natural choice for bringing learned scene representations into existing graphics workflows.Triangle- and mesh-based neural representations.()Blender Foundation, 2026()Unity Technologies, 2026

To exploit this support, triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering methods optimize geometry directly represented by triangle primitives . These approaches use either with independent faces or with shared vertices and explicit connectivity. 2DTS and Triangle-Splatting optimize independent triangles with soft coverage and alpha blending, DiffSoup uses neural texture features and a color decoder, and MeshSplatting introduces shared-vertex connectivity. Tab.  summarizes and contrasts the key design features across these representations alongside reference Gaussian baselines. These works demonstrate the potential of triangle- and mesh-based representations for high-quality NVS and offer promising routes toward graphics-engine integration.(; ; ; )Held et al., 2026bSheng et al., 2025Held et al., 2026aTojo et al., 2026triangle soupsindexed meshes()Sheng et al., 2025()Held et al., 2026b()Tojo et al., 2026()Held et al., 2026a1

However, using triangle primitives alone does ensure complete engine compatibility, as method-specific appearance and transparency models may still require additional adaptation. These methods are also developed and reported under different evaluation pipelines, making direct cross-method comparison difficult. Their original evaluations primarily use research-oriented source renderers rather than assess the learned representations after deployment in a graphics engine. MeshSuite addresses both gaps through unified evaluation and explicit graphics-engine deployment.not

Existing frameworks have sought to improve the reproducibility and comparability of NVS. Nerfstudio and GauStudio provide modular research frameworks for NeRF and Gaussian Splatting, while gsplat offers an efficient Gaussian rasterization library with extensive performance evaluations. More directly, NerfBaselines standardizes datasets, evaluation protocols, and metrics across NeRF and 3DGS methods while preserving their original implementations. Splatwizard further provides a specialized benchmark for 3DGS compression, evaluating rendering fidelity, computational efficiency, and geometric accuracy. The nvs-bench project facilitates reproducible NVS comparisons across different representations, including Triangle Splatting . Complementary studies investigate perceptual rendering quality and robustness under corrupted observations .Neural rendering benchmarks.()Tancik et al., 2023()Ye et al., 2024()Ye et al., 2025()Kulhanek and Sattler, 2025()Liu et al., 2026()nvs-bench contributors, 2026()Held et al., 2026b()Liang et al., 2024()Wang et al., 2024

Despite these efforts, existing benchmarks primarily focus on reconstruction quality and rendering efficiency within research-oriented source renderers, leaving graphics-engine deployment largely unexplored. MeshSuite addresses this gap by extending the evaluation of triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering to graphics-engine deployment, alongside a structural assessment of reconstructed meshes.

3

MeshSuite provides an end-to-end benchmark spanning evaluation with official Source Renderers and deployment in graphics engines. As illustrated in Fig. , it evaluates each trained representation under matched camera views, backgrounds, and evaluation metrics across three settings: Source Renderer, Standard Mesh Deployment, and Custom Engine Deployment. Comparisons across these settings reveal how graphics-engine deployment affects visual fidelity and rendering efficiency. For exported indexed meshes, we also assess structural usability, including local/global connectivity and manifoldness. Fig.  provides a more detailed overview of MeshSuite’s software architecture.16

3.1

Fair cross-method comparisons require consistent data and evaluation settings . MeshSuite standardizes three aspects:(; )Kulhanek and Sattler, 2025Liu et al., 2026

We standardize all methods to the white-background protocol for masked objects. 3.2

Existing triangle- and mesh-based methods encode geometry, appearance, and opacity in method-specific ways (Tab. ). For example, 2DTS and Triangle-Splatting use independent triangles with learned opacity, MeshSplatting uses shared vertices with view-dependent appearance, and DiffSoup represents appearance through learned features and a neural decoder. Engine deployment therefore requires method-specific interpretation of the trained model’s parameters.1()Sheng et al., 2025()Held et al., 2026b()Held et al., 2026a()Tojo et al., 2026

To support deployment through a common interface, MeshSuite introduces a implemented by an adapter for method . For each trained model , the adapter maps its parameters to an engine asset that follows the unified interface:translation layerℰm\mathcal{E}_{m}mm𝒮m\mathcal{S}_{m}𝒜m\mathcal{A}_{m}

The asset covers geometry, appearance, and opacity for different mesh structures. Translation decodes the trained model before deployment, allowing the engine to consume the exported asset independently of the training framework. The asset supplies the geometry and appearance data used by Standard Mesh Deployment and Custom Engine Deployment (see Appendix Fig. ).6

3.3

As illustrated in Fig. , MeshSuite organizes rendering into three evaluation settings: Standard Mesh Deployment, Custom Engine Deployment, and the reference Source Renderer. The Source Renderer serves as the baseline for the two engine-deployment settings.1

We render representations as conventional opaque meshes with static vertex colors and hardware Z-buffering. This setting omits method-specific shaders, neural decoders, and alpha blending. DiffSoup is unavailable in this setting.Standard Mesh Deployment ():𝐈mstd\mathbf{I}^{\mathrm{std}}_{m}

These differences affect transparency and view-dependent appearance, particularly for large or oblique primitives, and contribute to the adaptation gap.Differences from Source Renderer.

MeshSuite groups evaluation metrics into three categories: NVS quality, mesh quality, and computational cost.

Following Sec. , we report PSNR , SSIM , and LPIPS (VGG backbone, normalized images). 3.4.2

We evaluate Chamfer Distance (CD) on DTU, which adopts standard pipelines to isolate the object surface, complementing the white-background image protocol in Sec. .Surface geometry:3.1

Rendering as triangles does not guarantee a valid geometric surface. Let , , and denote the sets of unique vertices, undirected edges, and triangular faces in an exported mesh, with denoting set cardinality. We audit three complementary aspects:Mesh structural integrity:𝐕\mathbf{V}𝐄\mathbf{E}𝐅\mathbf{F}|⋅||\cdot|

    The boundary-edge and non-manifold-edge ratios are and , where and contain edges incident to one and more than two faces, respectively. The non-manifold-vertex ratio is , where is the set of vertices whose incident faces fail to form a single valid fan. Valid fans may be closed around an interior vertex or open at a boundary while disconnected fans are non-manifold. (see Fig.  for illustration).Local structure.|𝐄1|/|𝐄||\mathbf{E}_{1}|/|\mathbf{E}||𝐄>2|/|𝐄||\mathbf{E}_{>2}|/|\mathbf{E}|𝐄1\mathbf{E}_{1}𝐄>2\mathbf{E}_{>2}|𝐕nm|/|𝐕||\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{nm}}|/|\mathbf{V}|𝐕nm\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{nm}}2

    Two faces are considered adjacent if they share an edge. LCC faces and LCC area report the fractions of faces and surface area in the largest connected component (LCC), while Components counts the edge-connected components. We read component counts together with LCC fractions and visual inspection to account for differences in scene size and resolution. These three groups distinguish vertex sharing, local manifoldness, and fragmentation. Appendix Sec.  gives the audit details.Global connectivity.C

    • 3.4.3

    We audit computational overhead across training and inference. During training, we track peak VRAM (MiB) and optimization time (min). During engine deployment, we report GPU frame latency, wall-clock throughput (FPS), and renderer graphics allocations (MiB) separately. We additionally report serialized asset size (MiB) to characterize storage requirements.

    4

    4.1

    We evaluate four representative triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering methods, covering different designs in geometry connectivity, opacity, and appearance (Tabs.  and ):Methods.12

  • •

    replaces Gaussian primitives with independent planar triangle facelets and renders them through differentiable alpha blending. Its opacity function is defined using barycentric coordinates, with a compactness parameter controlling the transition from diffuse splats toward sharper triangle surfaces.2DTS()Sheng et al., 2025

  • •

    directly optimizes independent triangles using a differentiable window function confined to each projected triangle. Learned opacity, view-dependent color, and depth-ordered alpha blending support image-based optimization, while adaptive densification and pruning refine the allocation of triangles.Triangle-Splatting()Held et al., 2026b

  • •

    represents scenes with a compact triangle soup carrying neural texture features and binary opacity. Stochastic opacity masking makes binary opacity trainable within a depth-tested rasterization pipeline, while a neural color decoder maps texture features to rendered colors.DiffSoup()Tojo et al., 2026

  • •

    constructs a shared-vertex mesh through restricted Delaunay triangulation and jointly refines geometry and per-vertex spherical-harmonic appearance. Opacity and window parameter schedules progressively guide optimization toward opaque triangles.MeshSplatting()Held et al., 2026a

    • The first three methods produce without explicit shared-vertex connectivity, whereas MeshSplatting produces an . We audit the structure of its exported mesh in Sec. . We additionally include 3DGS and 2DGS as Gaussian-based reference baselines.triangle soupsindexed mesh4.4()Kerbl et al., 2023()Huang et al., 2024

    We evaluate on four complementary datasets spanning real-world environments and object-centric captures:Datasets.

  • •

    comprises nine real scenes, with surrounding camera trajectories, cluttered geometry, and large depth variations that challenge reconstruction of both foreground and distant content.Mip-NeRF 360()Barron et al., 2022

  • •

    For , we use the two outdoor scenes and , featuring large real-world objects, complex backgrounds, and occlusions.Tanks and Temples()Knapitsch et al., 2017traintruck

  • •

    provides laboratory captures of varied objects from 49 or 64 calibrated camera positions per scene, together with structured-light reference scans, enabling geometric evaluation alongside image fidelity.DTU()Jensen et al., 2014

  • •

    contains eight object-centric scenes with detailed geometry and realistic non-Lambertian materials, complementary to real captures.NeRF-Synthetic()Mildenhall et al., 2020

    • We follow the original training pipelines while applying the shared data and evaluation protocols. Images are downsampled according to each method’s requirements. All training and evaluation use a single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPU with 24 GB memory.Implementation details.

    End-to-end FPS includes CPU processing and GPU rendering. We also report GPU median (P50) and 95th-percentile (P95) frame latency, together with renderer graphics allocations.Timing and resource measurements.

    Before comparing methods, we check our reproductions against published results and public codebases. Across all 27 Mip-NeRF 360 method–scene pairs with published per-scene results, the mean absolute PSNR difference is only 0.075 dB and the maximum relative deviation is below 0.8%. Fig.  shows this close agreement in image quality. Appendix Tab.  provides dataset-level comparisons against paper values and public-code results.Reproducibility.37

    4.2

    Tab.  reports the standardized Source Renderer results across all four datasets. On Mip-NeRF 360 , NeRF-Synthetic , and DTU , 2DTS achieves the highest PSNR (28.16 dB, 33.65 dB, and 29.66 dB), while using the least peak training memory on NeRF-Synthetic and DTU (3172 MiB and 2470 MiB). Triangle-Splatting achieves the lowest LPIPS on Tanks and Temples (0.171) and DTU (0.080). DiffSoup renders and trains fastest on three datasets (up to 371 FPS and 12.216.8 min), but has lower image quality (18.90 dB on Tanks and Temples). MeshSplatting uses shared-vertex connectivity and trains fastest on DTU (10.7 min), with lower PSNR on Mip-NeRF 360 (24.72 dB). Thus, representation dominates fidelity, throughput, memory, and training time simultaneously.3()Barron et al., 2022()Mildenhall et al., 2020()Jensen et al., 2014∼\simno

    DTU complements NVS metrics with surface accuracy against reference scans (Tab. ). Results show that image quality and surface accuracy do not always yield the same ranking. While 2DTS leads in both PSNR (29.66 dB) and CD (0.63 mm), Triangle-Splatting achieves the lowest LPIPS (0.080) with a higher CD of 1.27 mm. MeshSplatting has similar PSNR to Triangle-Splatting (27.82 vs. 27.78 dB) but lower surface error (0.80 mm CD), while DiffSoup has the highest CD (3.89 mm). These results motivate evaluating image quality and surface geometry jointly before graphics deployment.2D novel-view fidelity vs. 3D surface geometry.3

    4.3

    Tab.  compares quality and throughput across the three settings on Mip-NeRF 360 and Tanks and Temples; Appendix Fig.  summarizes the PSNR trajectories of the four triangle- and mesh-based methods. Appendix Tab.  retains their per-scene Tanks and Temples results. Under our deployment protocol, 3DGS is unsupported in both engine settings; 2DGS lacks Custom Engine Deployment because TSDF meshing discards appearance variables used by the Source Renderer (though its mesh runs under Standard Mesh Deployment); and DiffSoup lacks a Standard Mesh Deployment opaque path because of its neural feature decoder.4712()Kerbl et al., 2023()Huang et al., 2024

    The evaluated triangle- and mesh-based methods rely on specialized appearance models or compositing operations that limit their direct compatibility with conventional opaque mesh pipelines. Our Standard Mesh Deployment tests this compatibility using static vertex colors and hardware Z-buffering. Methods that depend on rendering operations beyond this pipeline can lose substantial image quality when adapted to it.Deployment quality.

    On Mip-NeRF 360, adapting 2DTS, Triangle-Splatting, and MeshSplatting to Standard Mesh Deployment lowers mean PSNR by 15.64 dB, 12.36 dB, and 4.89 dB, respectively, relative to the Source Renderer (Tab. ). MeshSplatting has the smallest overall deployment gap () among these three methods. The rendered examples illustrate the visual losses: 2DTS produces large opaque shards on , and Triangle-Splatting exhibits a similar failure on (Fig. ).4Δ​Qmdeploy\Delta Q_{m}^{\mathrm{deploy}}bonsaitreehill4

    We implement method-specific Unity renderers for Custom Engine Deployment to retain each method’s appearance and compositing features. On Mip-NeRF 360, these implementations recover 2.6910.76 dB PSNR over Standard Mesh Deployment across 2DTS, Triangle-Splatting, and MeshSplatting, corresponding to their portability gaps (). They still fall short of the Source Renderer: the remaining adaptation losses () are 4.88 dB for 2DTS, 4.17 dB for Triangle-Splatting, and 2.20 dB for MeshSplatting. Appendix Fig.  shows these changes across the three settings.∼\simΔ​Qmport\Delta Q_{m}^{\mathrm{port}}Δ​Qmadapt\Delta Q_{m}^{\mathrm{adapt}}7

    For DiffSoup, our Custom Engine Deployment retains the color decoder required by its neural texture features, while DiffSoup is unsupported under the Standard Mesh Deployment protocol (marked N/A in Fig. ). Custom Engine Deployment achieves a mean PSNR of 23.15 dB on Mip-NeRF 360, compared with 23.54 dB for the Source Renderer (Tab. ). The example shows visually similar results in the two settings. Thin structures such as brake cables remain poorly resolved in both, so these artifacts cannot be attributed solely to engine deployment. Supplementary videos compare the rendering settings.44bicycle

    As a complementary baseline to the triangle- and mesh-based methods, 2DGS exhibits the inverse deployment trade-off of DiffSoup: while 2DGS achieves high visual fidelity in its Source Renderer (27.02 dB PSNR on Mip-NeRF 360, Tab. ), it is incompatible with Custom Engine Deployment () because TSDF-based mesh reconstruction strips the 2D Gaussian splatting primitives and opacity blending models required by custom engine rendering. Under Standard Mesh Deployment, the extracted TSDF mesh can be natively rasterized at over 4000 FPS, but experiences severe visual degradation (dropping to 12.37 dB PSNR). Appendix Sec.  and Fig.  provide qualitative comparisons on the scene illustrating the loss of specular highlights and geometry oversmoothing under standard rasterization.()Huang et al., 20244N/AE8counter

    The leading method depends on the dataset and deployment setting. Under Custom Engine Deployment, 2DTS has the highest PSNR on Mip-NeRF 360, while Triangle-Splatting leads on Tanks and Temples in all three image metrics (19.54 dB PSNR, 0.719 SSIM, and 0.258 LPIPS). DiffSoup has the highest Custom Engine Deployment throughput on both datasets, reaching 2388 FPS on Tanks and Temples. Among the four triangle- and mesh-based methods, MeshSplatting achieves the best Standard Mesh Deployment quality on both datasets; on Tanks and Temples, it reaches 14.38 dB PSNR, 0.506 SSIM, and 0.490 LPIPS. For the three methods available in both engine settings on Tanks and Temples, Custom Engine Deployment improves all three image metrics but reduces throughput by 5.17.3.Cross-dataset deployment behavior.∼\sim×\times

命中：neural rendering、rendering、mesh、splatting、rasterization

Triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering seeks to bridge neural representations and graphics engines through triangle primitives compatible with standard rasterization. Yet existing methods were developed and evaluated under inconsistent settings, with few direct comparisons and little evaluation in graphics engines. We introduce MeshSuite, the first benchmark for systematic evaluation of engine

License: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 arXiv:2609.01306v4 [cs.GR] 16 Oct 2026

MeshSuite: A Unified Benchmark for Triangle- and Mesh-Based Neural Rendering

Kaixuan Zhang Nanjing University of Science and Technology Affiliation: Minxian Li †Corresponding author.†thanks: Nanjing University of Science and Technology Affiliation: Mingwu Ren Nanjing University of Science and Technology Affiliation: Xiatian Zhu University of Surrey Affiliation: 

Abstract

Triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering aims to bridge neural scene representations and existing graphics engines (, Unity, Blender) by leveraging primitives compatible with standard rasterization hardware. There have been several such methods driven by parallel efforts, developed and evaluated under inconsistent settings, with little or no comparison with each other; critically, most even have never used graphics engines for evaluation nor considered deployability in practice – significantly undermining the objective and motivation. To address these issues, we introduce , the first benchmark of its kind to enable systematic evaluation of graphics-engine deployment and the reference Source Renderer for triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering methods. Importantly, our deployment protocol includes two engine deployment settings: (1) – a conventional opaque mesh pipeline with vertex colors and hardware Z-buffering; (2) – adding method-specific engine implementations supporting the retained appearance and compositing features (, alpha blending), so that the characteristics of each specific model can be taken into account. For mesh splatting, we further propose a structural audit of exported surfaces, diagnosing topological and geometric integrity toward downstream graphics assets. We highlight several results: (1) Graphics engine deployment would incur image-quality degradation under both deployment options. Among the triangle- and mesh-based NVS methods studied, MeshSplatting degrades the least under Standard Mesh Deployment. (2) The deployment setting matters – Custom Engine Deployment can retain the majority of fidelity at a roughly 533 slowdown relative to Standard Mesh Deployment across the two deployment datasets. (3) About mesh splatting, the current approaches to explicit connectivity and shared indexing are still limited: shared vertex indexing alone does not ensure manifoldness or global connectivity. From this benchmark, we validate that , and highlight the significance of assessing the graphics engine deployment process (, the degree of engine compatibility). The project page is accessible at .e.g.triangleMeshSuiteStandard Mesh DeploymentCustom Engine Deploymente.g.∼\sim×\timesrasterizability is merely part of graphics readinesse.g.https://surrey-up-lab.github.io/MeshSuite

1

Reconstructing a scene from multi-view images allows users to explore it from arbitrary viewpoints beyond those originally captured, supporting a wide range of vision and graphics applications, including AR/VR , gaming , and robotic perception . Recent advances in neural rendering, particularly Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) , have enabled increasingly realistic novel-view synthesis (NVS). Specifically, NeRFs use multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) to encode scene density and view-dependent color, synthesizing novel views through volume rendering . However, their practical use is constrained by high computational costs and the lack of an explicit geometric representation. In contrast, 3DGS represents scenes explicitly with 3D Gaussian primitives and uses efficient differentiable splatting to substantially reduce rendering costs .()Broxton et al., 2020()Lachambre et al., 2017()Zhu et al., 2022()Mildenhall et al., 2020()Kerbl et al., 2023()Mildenhall et al., 2020()Kerbl et al., 2023

Despite these advances, neither representation is directly compatible with the standard rendering pipelines of established computer graphics (CG) engines, such as Blender and Unity . These engines have benefited from decades of development and optimization, providing efficient rendering pipelines and integrated tools for lighting and shadows, material editing, and animation. Their mature ecosystems also offer extensive collections of reusable assets and plugins , facilitating the integration of reconstructed scenes into practical applications.()Blender Foundation, 2026()Unity Technologies, 2026(; )Unity Technologies, 2026Blender Foundation, 2026

To better take advantage of these engines, researchers have increasingly explored triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering methods, which optimize triangle primitives already supported by standard graphics hardware . These methods have demonstrated impressive NVS performance comparable to that of NeRFs and 3DGS, while offering a promising path toward integration with existing CG engines . However, existing triangle- and mesh-based works follow separate evaluation protocols, with differences in data preprocessing, image formats, evaluation metrics, and metric implementations, and none evaluates the methods in a graphics engine. Using triangles alone also does not ensure complete engine compatibility. Existing methods use triangles with substantially different features (Tab. ), including continuous or discrete opacity , coverage defined inside or outside a triangle , varying color representations (, view-dependent spherical harmonics (SHs) or neural networks ), and the presence or absence of neural texture decoders . These variations pose challenges for engine rendering and may require method-specific shaders, buffers, sorting strategies, and runtime state. Furthermore, existing mesh splatting methods evaluate exported mesh quality solely through vertex sharing, lacking a comprehensive analysis of critical structural and topological properties such as manifoldness and global connectivity.(; )Held et al., 2026bHeld et al., 2026a(; ; )Held et al., 2026bSheng et al., 2025Held et al., 2026a1(; )Held et al., 2026bHeld et al., 2026a(; )Sheng et al., 2025Held et al., 2026be.g.()Held et al., 2026a()Tojo et al., 2026(; )Tojo et al., 2026Held et al., 2026b()Held et al., 2026a

To address these questions, we introduce , a unified benchmark for evaluating triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering (see Fig. ). This benchmark enables: (a) integration of existing triangle- and mesh-based splatting methods; (b) fair and consistent comparison of different methods in a unified setting; (c) extensive evaluation of both triangle- and mesh-based models during training and inference; (d) Source Renderer evaluation and two engine deployment settings: - converting a trained model to a standard opaque vertex-colored mesh before rendering in a graphics engine; - adding a customized layer to implement method-specific designs, such as specialized appearance representations and alpha compositing.MeshSuite1Standard Mesh DeploymentCustom Engine Deployment

We note three key findings. , engine deployment reduces visual quality relative to the Source Renderer, with MeshSplatting losing the least quality under Standard Mesh Deployment among the studied methods (Tab. ). Second, Custom Engine Deployment produces more visually appealing renderings than Standard Mesh Deployment, at the cost of a roughly 533 slowdown (Tab. ). Third, existing mesh splatting methods’ exported meshes exhibit non-manifold structures and substantial fragmentation (Tab. ). These results show that ; appearance preservation, efficiency, and mesh structure must be evaluated together.First()Held et al., 2026a4∼\sim×\times46using triangles alone does not ensure graphics readiness

Our are as follows: () the first unified benchmark, , for evaluating triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering methods; () Custom Engine Deployment of existing methods in a graphics engine (, Unity), retaining their specific designs during engine rendering; and () an extensive evaluation of existing models in terms of novel-view synthesis, training/inference cost, and mesh structure.contributionsIMeshSuiteIIi.e.III

2

Novel-view synthesis (NVS) aims to synthesize images of a scene from viewpoints beyond those observed in the input images. A central component of this task is a scene representation that captures both geometry and appearance. NeRF represents a scene as a continuous function and synthesize views through volumetric integration . Later methods improve reconstruction quality and anti-aliasing or accelerate rendering through explicit, factorized, and hashed structures . 3DGS replaces repeated network queries with optimized anisotropic Gaussian primitives and a dedicated splatting rasterizer . Follow-up works refine Gaussian optimization or encourages surface-aligned geometry . These methods establish strong NVS baselines, but their representations are not natively supported by conventional graphics engines (, Unity and Blender). Integration with existing CG engines therefore requires specialized rendering implementations or conversion to mesh-based assets.Dominant neural representations.()Mildenhall et al., 2020(; ; )Barron et al., 2021Barron et al., 2022Barron et al., 2023(; ; ; ; )Reiser et al., 2024Yu et al., 2021Fridovich-Keil et al., 2022Chen et al., 2022Müller et al., 2022()Kerbl et al., 2023(; ; )Kheradmand et al., 2024Huang et al., 2024Guédon and Lepetit, 2024e.g.

To facilitate integration with conventional graphics engines, methods such as MobileNeRF and BakedSDF convert learned radiance fields into mesh-based representations. For explicit splats, SuGaR and GaMeS extract mesh surfaces from 3D Gaussian primitives or bind Gaussian primitives to deformable mesh faces. Although these conversion pipelines produce standard mesh assets, they often rely on lossy post-processing (, Marching Cubes, Poisson surface reconstruction, or heuristic simplification) that decouples the optimization target from the final rendering objective.()Chen et al., 2023()Yariv et al., 2023()Guédon and Lepetit, 2024()Waczyńska et al., 2024e.g.

Established CG engines, such as Blender and Unity , provide optimized rendering pipelines and integrated tools for scene editing, lighting, and animation, together with mature ecosystems of reusable assets and plugins. Triangle meshes are widely supported by these pipelines, making them a natural choice for bringing learned scene representations into existing graphics workflows.Triangle- and mesh-based neural representations.()Blender Foundation, 2026()Unity Technologies, 2026

To exploit this support, triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering methods optimize geometry directly represented by triangle primitives . These approaches use either with independent faces or with shared vertices and explicit connectivity. 2DTS and Triangle-Splatting optimize independent triangles with soft coverage and alpha blending, DiffSoup uses neural texture features and a color decoder, and MeshSplatting introduces shared-vertex connectivity. Tab.  summarizes and contrasts the key design features across these representations alongside reference Gaussian baselines. These works demonstrate the potential of triangle- and mesh-based representations for high-quality NVS and offer promising routes toward graphics-engine integration.(; ; ; )Held et al., 2026bSheng et al., 2025Held et al., 2026aTojo et al., 2026triangle soupsindexed meshes()Sheng et al., 2025()Held et al., 2026b()Tojo et al., 2026()Held et al., 2026a1

However, using triangle primitives alone does ensure complete engine compatibility, as method-specific appearance and transparency models may still require additional adaptation. These methods are also developed and reported under different evaluation pipelines, making direct cross-method comparison difficult. Their original evaluations primarily use research-oriented source renderers rather than assess the learned representations after deployment in a graphics engine. MeshSuite addresses both gaps through unified evaluation and explicit graphics-engine deployment.not

Existing frameworks have sought to improve the reproducibility and comparability of NVS. Nerfstudio and GauStudio provide modular research frameworks for NeRF and Gaussian Splatting, while gsplat offers an efficient Gaussian rasterization library with extensive performance evaluations. More directly, NerfBaselines standardizes datasets, evaluation protocols, and metrics across NeRF and 3DGS methods while preserving their original implementations. Splatwizard further provides a specialized benchmark for 3DGS compression, evaluating rendering fidelity, computational efficiency, and geometric accuracy. The nvs-bench project facilitates reproducible NVS comparisons across different representations, including Triangle Splatting . Complementary studies investigate perceptual rendering quality and robustness under corrupted observations .Neural rendering benchmarks.()Tancik et al., 2023()Ye et al., 2024()Ye et al., 2025()Kulhanek and Sattler, 2025()Liu et al., 2026()nvs-bench contributors, 2026()Held et al., 2026b()Liang et al., 2024()Wang et al., 2024

Despite these efforts, existing benchmarks primarily focus on reconstruction quality and rendering efficiency within research-oriented source renderers, leaving graphics-engine deployment largely unexplored. MeshSuite addresses this gap by extending the evaluation of triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering to graphics-engine deployment, alongside a structural assessment of reconstructed meshes.

3

MeshSuite provides an end-to-end benchmark spanning evaluation with official Source Renderers and deployment in graphics engines. As illustrated in Fig. , it evaluates each trained representation under matched camera views, backgrounds, and evaluation metrics across three settings: Source Renderer, Standard Mesh Deployment, and Custom Engine Deployment. Comparisons across these settings reveal how graphics-engine deployment affects visual fidelity and rendering efficiency. For exported indexed meshes, we also assess structural usability, including local/global connectivity and manifoldness. Fig.  provides a more detailed overview of MeshSuite’s software architecture.16

3.1

Fair cross-method comparisons require consistent data and evaluation settings . MeshSuite standardizes three aspects:(; )Kulhanek and Sattler, 2025Liu et al., 2026

For a held-out camera set , the benchmark standardizes camera coordinate frames, optical axes, field of view, and projection matrices.Camera and viewpoint alignment:𝒞\mathcal{C}

We standardize all methods to the white-background protocol for masked objects. 3.2

Existing triangle- and mesh-based methods encode geometry, appearance, and opacity in method-specific ways (Tab. ). For example, 2DTS and Triangle-Splatting use independent triangles with learned opacity, MeshSplatting uses shared vertices with view-dependent appearance, and DiffSoup represents appearance through learned features and a neural decoder. Engine deployment therefore requires method-specific interpretation of the trained model’s parameters.1()Sheng et al., 2025()Held et al., 2026b()Held et al., 2026a()Tojo et al., 2026

To support deployment through a common interface, MeshSuite introduces a implemented by an adapter for method . For each trained model , the adapter maps its parameters to an engine asset that follows the unified interface:translation layerℰm\mathcal{E}_{m}mm𝒮m\mathcal{S}_{m}𝒜m\mathcal{A}_{m}

The asset covers geometry, appearance, and opacity for different mesh structures. Translation decodes the trained model before deployment, allowing the engine to consume the exported asset independently of the training framework. The asset supplies the geometry and appearance data used by Standard Mesh Deployment and Custom Engine Deployment (see Appendix Fig. ).6

3.3

As illustrated in Fig. , MeshSuite organizes rendering into three evaluation settings: Standard Mesh Deployment, Custom Engine Deployment, and the reference Source Renderer. The Source Renderer serves as the baseline for the two engine-deployment settings.1

We render representations as conventional opaque meshes with static vertex colors and hardware Z-buffering. This setting omits method-specific shaders, neural decoders, and alpha blending. DiffSoup is unavailable in this setting.Standard Mesh Deployment ():𝐈mstd\mathbf{I}^{\mathrm{std}}_{m}

MeshSuite groups evaluation metrics into three categories: NVS quality, mesh quality, and computational cost.

3.4.1

Following Sec. , we report PSNR , SSIM , and LPIPS (VGG backbone, normalized images). 3.4.2

We evaluate Chamfer Distance (CD) on DTU, which adopts standard pipelines to isolate the object surface, complementing the white-background image protocol in Sec. .Surface geometry:3.1

Rendering as triangles does not guarantee a valid geometric surface. Let , , and denote the sets of unique vertices, undirected edges, and triangular faces in an exported mesh, with denoting set cardinality. We audit three complementary aspects:Mesh structural integrity:𝐕\mathbf{V}𝐄\mathbf{E}𝐅\mathbf{F}|⋅||\cdot|

  • •

    The ratio (abbreviated as V/F in tables) measures unique vertices per face, and average valence summarizes local adjacency density. With a common export convention, lower indicates greater vertex sharing.Local reuse.|𝐕|/|𝐅||\mathbf{V}|/|\mathbf{F}|2​|𝐄|/|𝐕|2|\mathbf{E}|/|\mathbf{V}||𝐕|/|𝐅||\mathbf{V}|/|\mathbf{F}|

  • •

    The boundary-edge and non-manifold-edge ratios are and , where and contain edges incident to one and more than two faces, respectively. The non-manifold-vertex ratio is , where is the set of vertices whose incident faces fail to form a single valid fan. Valid fans may be closed around an interior vertex or open at a boundary while disconnected fans are non-manifold. (see Fig.  for illustration).Local structure.|𝐄1|/|𝐄||\mathbf{E}_{1}|/|\mathbf{E}||𝐄>2|/|𝐄||\mathbf{E}_{>2}|/|\mathbf{E}|𝐄1\mathbf{E}_{1}𝐄>2\mathbf{E}_{>2}|𝐕nm|/|𝐕||\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{nm}}|/|\mathbf{V}|𝐕nm\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{nm}}2

  • •

    Two faces are considered adjacent if they share an edge. LCC faces and LCC area report the fractions of faces and surface area in the largest connected component (LCC), while Components counts the edge-connected components. We read component counts together with LCC fractions and visual inspection to account for differences in scene size and resolution. These three groups distinguish vertex sharing, local manifoldness, and fragmentation. Appendix Sec.  gives the audit details.Global connectivity.C

    • 3.4.3

    We audit computational overhead across training and inference. During training, we track peak VRAM (MiB) and optimization time (min). During engine deployment, we report GPU frame latency, wall-clock throughput (FPS), and renderer graphics allocations (MiB) separately. We additionally report serialized asset size (MiB) to characterize storage requirements.

    4

    4.1

    We evaluate four representative triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering methods, covering different designs in geometry connectivity, opacity, and appearance (Tabs.  and ):Methods.12

  • •

    replaces Gaussian primitives with independent planar triangle facelets and renders them through differentiable alpha blending. Its opacity function is defined using barycentric coordinates, with a compactness parameter controlling the transition from diffuse splats toward sharper triangle surfaces.2DTS()Sheng et al., 2025

  • •

    directly optimizes independent triangles using a differentiable window function confined to each projected triangle. Learned opacity, view-dependent color, and depth-ordered alpha blending support image-based optimization, while adaptive densification and pruning refine the allocation of triangles.Triangle-Splatting()Held et al., 2026b

  • •

    represents scenes with a compact triangle soup carrying neural texture features and binary opacity. Stochastic opacity masking makes binary opacity trainable within a depth-tested rasterization pipeline, while a neural color decoder maps texture features to rendered colors.DiffSoup()Tojo et al., 2026

  • •

    constructs a shared-vertex mesh through restricted Delaunay triangulation and jointly refines geometry and per-vertex spherical-harmonic appearance. Opacity and window parameter schedules progressively guide optimization toward opaque triangles.MeshSplatting()Held et al., 2026a

    • The first three methods produce without explicit shared-vertex connectivity, whereas MeshSplatting produces an . We audit the structure of its exported mesh in Sec. . We additionally include 3DGS and 2DGS as Gaussian-based reference baselines.triangle soupsindexed mesh4.4()Kerbl et al., 2023()Huang et al., 2024

    We evaluate on four complementary datasets spanning real-world environments and object-centric captures:Datasets.

  • •

    comprises nine real scenes, with surrounding camera trajectories, cluttered geometry, and large depth variations that challenge reconstruction of both foreground and distant content.Mip-NeRF 360()Barron et al., 2022

  • •

    For , we use the two outdoor scenes and , featuring large real-world objects, complex backgrounds, and occlusions.Tanks and Temples()Knapitsch et al., 2017traintruck

  • •

    provides laboratory captures of varied objects from 49 or 64 calibrated camera positions per scene, together with structured-light reference scans, enabling geometric evaluation alongside image fidelity.DTU()Jensen et al., 2014

  • •

    contains eight object-centric scenes with detailed geometry and realistic non-Lambertian materials, complementary to real captures.NeRF-Synthetic()Mildenhall et al., 2020

    • We follow the original training pipelines while applying the shared data and evaluation protocols. Images are downsampled according to each method’s requirements. All training and evaluation use a single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPU with 24 GB memory.Implementation details.

    End-to-end FPS includes CPU processing and GPU rendering. We also report GPU median (P50) and 95th-percentile (P95) frame latency, together with renderer graphics allocations.Timing and resource measurements.

    Before comparing methods, we check our reproductions against published results and public codebases. Across all 27 Mip-NeRF 360 method–scene pairs with published per-scene results, the mean absolute PSNR difference is only 0.075 dB and the maximum relative deviation is below 0.8%. Fig.  shows this close agreement in image quality. Appendix Tab.  provides dataset-level comparisons against paper values and public-code results.Reproducibility.37

    4.2

    Tab.  reports the standardized Source Renderer results across all four datasets. On Mip-NeRF 360 , NeRF-Synthetic , and DTU , 2DTS achieves the highest PSNR (28.16 dB, 33.65 dB, and 29.66 dB), while using the least peak training memory on NeRF-Synthetic and DTU (3172 MiB and 2470 MiB). Triangle-Splatting achieves the lowest LPIPS on Tanks and Temples (0.171) and DTU (0.080). DiffSoup renders and trains fastest on three datasets (up to 371 FPS and 12.216.8 min), but has lower image quality (18.90 dB on Tanks and Temples). MeshSplatting uses shared-vertex connectivity and trains fastest on DTU (10.7 min), with lower PSNR on Mip-NeRF 360 (24.72 dB). Thus, representation dominates fidelity, throughput, memory, and training time simultaneously.3()Barron et al., 2022()Mildenhall et al., 2020()Jensen et al., 2014∼\simno

    DTU complements NVS metrics with surface accuracy against reference scans (Tab. ). Results show that image quality and surface accuracy do not always yield the same ranking. While 2DTS leads in both PSNR (29.66 dB) and CD (0.63 mm), Triangle-Splatting achieves the lowest LPIPS (0.080) with a higher CD of 1.27 mm. MeshSplatting has similar PSNR to Triangle-Splatting (27.82 vs. 27.78 dB) but lower surface error (0.80 mm CD), while DiffSoup has the highest CD (3.89 mm). These results motivate evaluating image quality and surface geometry jointly before graphics deployment.2D novel-view fidelity vs. 3D surface geometry.3

    4.3

    Tab.  compares quality and throughput across the three settings on Mip-NeRF 360 and Tanks and Temples; Appendix Fig.  summarizes the PSNR trajectories of the four triangle- and mesh-based methods. Appendix Tab.  retains their per-scene Tanks and Temples results. Under our deployment protocol, 3DGS is unsupported in both engine settings; 2DGS lacks Custom Engine Deployment because TSDF meshing discards appearance variables used by the Source Renderer (though its mesh runs under Standard Mesh Deployment); and DiffSoup lacks a Standard Mesh Deployment opaque path because of its neural feature decoder.4712()Kerbl et al., 2023()Huang et al., 2024

    The evaluated triangle- and mesh-based methods rely on specialized appearance models or compositing operations that limit their direct compatibility with conventional opaque mesh pipelines. Our Standard Mesh Deployment tests this compatibility using static vertex colors and hardware Z-buffering. Methods that depend on rendering operations beyond this pipeline can lose substantial image quality when adapted to it.Deployment quality.

    On Mip-NeRF 360, adapting 2DTS, Triangle-Splatting, and MeshSplatting to Standard Mesh Deployment lowers mean PSNR by 15.64 dB, 12.36 dB, and 4.89 dB, respectively, relative to the Source Renderer (Tab. ). MeshSplatting has the smallest overall deployment gap () among these three methods. The rendered examples illustrate the visual losses: 2DTS produces large opaque shards on , and Triangle-Splatting exhibits a similar failure on (Fig. ).4Δ​Qmdeploy\Delta Q_{m}^{\mathrm{deploy}}bonsaitreehill4

    We implement method-specific Unity renderers for Custom Engine Deployment to retain each method’s appearance and compositing features. On Mip-NeRF 360, these implementations recover 2.6910.76 dB PSNR over Standard Mesh Deployment across 2DTS, Triangle-Splatting, and MeshSplatting, corresponding to their portability gaps (). They still fall short of the Source Renderer: the remaining adaptation losses () are 4.88 dB for 2DTS, 4.17 dB for Triangle-Splatting, and 2.20 dB for MeshSplatting. Appendix Fig.  shows these changes across the three settings.∼\simΔ​Qmport\Delta Q_{m}^{\mathrm{port}}Δ​Qmadapt\Delta Q_{m}^{\mathrm{adapt}}7

    For DiffSoup, our Custom Engine Deployment retains the color decoder required by its neural texture features, while DiffSoup is unsupported under the Standard Mesh Deployment protocol (marked N/A in Fig. ). Custom Engine Deployment achieves a mean PSNR of 23.15 dB on Mip-NeRF 360, compared with 23.54 dB for the Source Renderer (Tab. ). The example shows visually similar results in the two settings. Thin structures such as brake cables remain poorly resolved in both, so these artifacts cannot be attributed solely to engine deployment. Supplementary videos compare the rendering settings.44bicycle

    As a complementary baseline to the triangle- and mesh-based methods, 2DGS exhibits the inverse deployment trade-off of DiffSoup: while 2DGS achieves high visual fidelity in its Source Renderer (27.02 dB PSNR on Mip-NeRF 360, Tab. ), it is incompatible with Custom Engine Deployment () because TSDF-based mesh reconstruction strips the 2D Gaussian splatting primitives and opacity blending models required by custom engine rendering. Under Standard Mesh Deployment, the extracted TSDF mesh can be natively rasterized at over 4000 FPS, but experiences severe visual degradation (dropping to 12.37 dB PSNR). Appendix Sec.  and Fig.  provide qualitative comparisons on the scene illustrating the loss of specular highlights and geometry oversmoothing under standard rasterization.()Huang et al., 20244N/AE8counter

    The leading method depends on the dataset and deployment setting. Under Custom Engine Deployment, 2DTS has the highest PSNR on Mip-NeRF 360, while Triangle-Splatting leads on Tanks and Temples in all three image metrics (19.54 dB PSNR, 0.719 SSIM, and 0.258 LPIPS). DiffSoup has the highest Custom Engine Deployment throughput on both datasets, reaching 2388 FPS on Tanks and Temples. Among the four triangle- and mesh-based methods, MeshSplatting achieves the best Standard Mesh Deployment quality on both datasets; on Tanks and Temples, it reaches 14.38 dB PSNR, 0.506 SSIM, and 0.490 LPIPS. For the three methods available in both engine settings on Tanks and Temples, Custom Engine Deployment improves all three image metrics but reduces throughput by 5.17.3.Cross-dataset deployment behavior.∼\sim×\times

item.title: AI Agent 工作流引擎工程实践：从 Prompt 清单到状态机驱动的生产级流程控制
item.description:
来源：掘金（中文） 相关度：14.2 正文：14410 字 / 0 图

命中：引擎、agent

凌晨 2 点，客服 Agent 在处理退款争议时崩溃了。 不是因为模型出了问题，而是因为它在第 7 步——调用支付系统 API 确认退款金额——收到了一个网络超时。没有断点续跑机制，整个工作流从头开始。但"从头开始"意味着它重新发起了一次退款请求。客户收到了两笔退款。

AI Agent 工作流引擎工程实践：从 Prompt 清单到状态机驱动的生产级流程控制

AINative软件工程 2026-10-20 0

你的 Agent 能干活，但它能可靠地干活吗？当工作流从 3 步扩展到 15 步，从 demo 走进生产，"Prompt 里写了规则"就不再够用。本文拆解 Agent 工作流引擎的核心设计模式、生产陷阱与选型决策框架。

一个真实的生产事故

凌晨 2 点，客服 Agent 在处理退款争议时崩溃了。

不是因为模型出了问题，而是因为它在第 7 步——调用支付系统 API 确认退款金额——收到了一个网络超时。没有断点续跑机制，整个工作流从头开始。但"从头开始"意味着它重新发起了一次退款请求。客户收到了两笔退款。

这不是假设场景。2026 年 Q3，我们团队在处理的一个 Agent 系统就踩了这个坑。根因很简单：工作流的状态只活在内存里，进程挂了，状态就没了。

这个问题在 Agent 工程社区里有一个正式的名字：。而围绕它的更大问题是：Agent 的工作流到底应该怎么管理？Durable Execution 缺失

Prompt 清单的天花板

大多数团队的 Agent 工作流管理方式是这样的：

# Agent 工作流规则（写在 System Prompt 里）

1. 先分析用户需求，生成分析计划
2. 按计划执行每一步
3. 每步执行后验证结果
4. 如果验证失败，重试最多 3 次
5. 所有步骤完成后生成总结报告
6. 遇到敏感操作（删除、支付、发邮件），等待人工确认

这种方式能跑，但它有三个致命问题：

当 context window 被工具调用的输出塞满，System Prompt 里的规则会被注意力机制"稀释"。我们实测过一个 7 步工作流：在步骤 5 之后，Agent 跳过验证步骤直接给出结论的概率从 2% 上升到 34%。第一，Agent 会"忘记"规则。

Prompt 说"先分析再执行"，但 Agent 完全可以跳过分析直接动手——它只是在文本层面"同意"了规则，运行时没有任何东西阻止它偏离流程。第二，没有强制的状态转移。

"重试 3 次"写在 Prompt 里，但重试的计数器也在 Prompt 管理的 context 里。Agent 可能记错重试次数，或者把不同任务的重试次数混在一起。第三，失败路径不可控。

这不是 Prompt 的错。Prompt 擅长描述意图，不擅长强制执行流程。

状态机：把工作流从"建议"变成"法律"

2026 年 Agent 工程社区的一个明确趋势是：。用有限状态机（FSM）来管理 Agent 的工作流

核心思路很直接：把工作流的每个阶段定义为一个状态，状态之间的转移需要满足特定条件（gate），每个状态产出必须附带可验证的证据（evidence）。

一个典型的 Agent 工作流状态机：

┌─────────┐    task contract    ┌──────────┐    scoped plan    ┌─────────────┐
│    │ ─────────────────→ │      │ ────────────────→ │    │
└─────────┘                     └──────────┘                    └──────┬──────┘
    ↑                              ↑ revise                           │

    生产环境的 5 个工程陷阱

    陷阱 1：Checkpoint 粒度不对

    最常见的错误是只在状态转移时 checkpoint。如果某个步骤执行了 5 分钟，在第 4 分钟崩溃了，那 4 分钟的工作就白做了。

    正确做法是区分 （状态转移时保存）和 （关键操作前后保存）：粗粒度 checkpoint细粒度 checkpoint

}

    一个真实数据：我们把 checkpoint 粒度从"每状态"改为"每操作"后，工作流的平均恢复时间从 3.2 分钟降到 12 秒。

    陷阱 2：状态爆炸

    当工作流的条件分支超过 8 个时，状态数量会以指数级增长。一个原本 6 步的线性流程，加上各种异常路径后，可能膨胀到 40+ 个状态。

    解法是 ：把复杂工作流拆成子工作流，每个子工作流有自己的状态机，父工作流只管理子工作流之间的转移。分层状态机

    陷阱 3：证据验证变成了形式主义

    状态机要求每个状态转移时提交证据，但如果证据验证太松，Agent 就会学会"应付检查"——生成一份看起来像回事但实际上没用的证据。

    陷阱 4：重试风暴

    当一个步骤失败并触发重试时，如果上游有多个实例同时重试，可能形成"重试风暴"——所有实例在同一时刻对同一个下游服务发起请求。

    陷阱 5：工作流版本管理的缺失

    这是最容易被忽视的陷阱。工作流定义修改了（比如新增了一个验证步骤），但还有 50 个正在进行中的工作流实例运行的是旧版本。新版本部署后，这些实例从 checkpoint 恢复时，发现状态机结构变了，直接崩溃。

    决策框架：什么时候用状态机，什么时候不用

    不是所有 Agent 任务都适合状态机管理。过度工程化同样有害。

    适合状态机的场景：

  • 流程步骤确定，可以提前枚举
  • 步骤之间有明确的先后依赖
  • 失败的代价高（支付、数据删除、外部通知）
  • 需要审计日志和合规记录
  • 多步骤的 CRUD 操作链

    • 不适合状态机的场景：

  • 探索性研究（"帮我调研 XX 领域的最新进展"）
  • 开放式头脑风暴
  • 调试和问题诊断（失败模式未知）
  • 单步骤的简单任务
  • 需要 Agent 自主决定流程走向的创新任务

    • 一个实用的判断标准：如果你能画出这个任务的工作流图，它就适合状态机管理；如果你画不出来，就别硬画。

    可观测性：工作流引擎不是黑盒

    工作流引擎的每一步都应该产生可观测性数据。三个关键指标：

    1. 状态转移延迟（State Transition Latency）

    每个状态的平均停留时间。如果某个状态的 p99 延迟突然飙升，说明这个步骤的下游可能出了问题。

    metrics.(, duration, {
  : workflowId,
  : state.,
  : workflowVersion,
});
histogram'workflow.state_duration_ms'workflow_idstatenameversion

    2. 转移成功率（Transition Success Rate）

    每个状态的转移成功/失败比例。如果某个状态的成功率低于阈值，触发告警。

    3. Checkpoint 大小增长率（Checkpoint Growth Rate）

    如果 checkpoint 数据增长过快，说明 context 在膨胀，可能需要做 context 裁剪。我们见过一个案例，checkpoint 从 2KB 增长到 12MB，导致恢复时间从毫秒级变成秒级。

    写在最后

    Agent 工作流引擎不是一个新概念——传统工作流引擎（Airflow、Temporal、Camunda）已经存在了很多年。但 Agent 时代的工作流引擎需要解决一个传统引擎不需要面对的问题：。执行者（LLM）是非确定性的

    传统工作流引擎假设每个步骤的执行结果是确定的（给定相同的输入）。Agent 不是。同一个 Prompt、同一个上下文，Agent 可能产出不同的结果。这意味着工作流引擎的 gate 验证、证据检查、重试策略都需要为这种不确定性做额外设计。

    2026 年的趋势很明确：Agent 工作流正在从"Prompt 描述"走向"代码强制"。LangGraph 提供了图结构，Temporal 提供了持久化执行，新兴方案提供了可验证执行。选择哪个取决于你的场景复杂度、可靠性要求和团队技术栈。

    但无论选择哪个方向，核心原则不变：流程应该在代码里，而不是在 Prompt 的想象里。

    参考来源：

  • Aharness (GitHub): 工作流的有限状态机实现
  • LangGraph 文档：Graph-based agent orchestration
  • Temporal 文档：Durable execution for long-running workflows
  • Developer's Digest: "Agent Workflows as Code: Why State Machines Beat Prompt Checklists" (2026-06)
  • LangChain Blog: "How to Build a Custom Agent Harness" (2026)

命中：引擎、agent

凌晨 2 点，客服 Agent 在处理退款争议时崩溃了。 不是因为模型出了问题，而是因为它在第 7 步——调用支付系统 API 确认退款金额——收到了一个网络超时。没有断点续跑机制，整个工作流从头开始。但"从头开始"意味着它重新发起了一次退款请求。客户收到了两笔退款。

AI Agent 工作流引擎工程实践：从 Prompt 清单到状态机驱动的生产级流程控制

AINative软件工程 2026-10-20 0

你的 Agent 能干活，但它能可靠地干活吗？当工作流从 3 步扩展到 15 步，从 demo 走进生产，"Prompt 里写了规则"就不再够用。本文拆解 Agent 工作流引擎的核心设计模式、生产陷阱与选型决策框架。

一个真实的生产事故

凌晨 2 点，客服 Agent 在处理退款争议时崩溃了。

不是因为模型出了问题，而是因为它在第 7 步——调用支付系统 API 确认退款金额——收到了一个网络超时。没有断点续跑机制，整个工作流从头开始。但"从头开始"意味着它重新发起了一次退款请求。客户收到了两笔退款。

这不是假设场景。2026 年 Q3，我们团队在处理的一个 Agent 系统就踩了这个坑。根因很简单：工作流的状态只活在内存里，进程挂了，状态就没了。

这个问题在 Agent 工程社区里有一个正式的名字：。而围绕它的更大问题是：Agent 的工作流到底应该怎么管理？Durable Execution 缺失

Prompt 清单的天花板

大多数团队的 Agent 工作流管理方式是这样的：

# Agent 工作流规则（写在 System Prompt 里）

1. 先分析用户需求，生成分析计划
2. 按计划执行每一步
3. 每步执行后验证结果
4. 如果验证失败，重试最多 3 次
5. 所有步骤完成后生成总结报告
6. 遇到敏感操作（删除、支付、发邮件），等待人工确认

这种方式能跑，但它有三个致命问题：

当 context window 被工具调用的输出塞满，System Prompt 里的规则会被注意力机制"稀释"。我们实测过一个 7 步工作流：在步骤 5 之后，Agent 跳过验证步骤直接给出结论的概率从 2% 上升到 34%。第一，Agent 会"忘记"规则。

Prompt 说"先分析再执行"，但 Agent 完全可以跳过分析直接动手——它只是在文本层面"同意"了规则，运行时没有任何东西阻止它偏离流程。第二，没有强制的状态转移。

"重试 3 次"写在 Prompt 里，但重试的计数器也在 Prompt 管理的 context 里。Agent 可能记错重试次数，或者把不同任务的重试次数混在一起。第三，失败路径不可控。

这不是 Prompt 的错。Prompt 擅长描述意图，不擅长强制执行流程。

状态机：把工作流从"建议"变成"法律"

2026 年 Agent 工程社区的一个明确趋势是：。用有限状态机（FSM）来管理 Agent 的工作流

核心思路很直接：把工作流的每个阶段定义为一个状态，状态之间的转移需要满足特定条件（gate），每个状态产出必须附带可验证的证据（evidence）。

一个典型的 Agent 工作流状态机：

┌─────────┐    task contract    ┌──────────┐    scoped plan    ┌─────────────┐
│    │ ─────────────────→ │      │ ────────────────→ │    │

    生产环境的 5 个工程陷阱

    陷阱 1：Checkpoint 粒度不对

    陷阱 2：状态爆炸

    当工作流的条件分支超过 8 个时，状态数量会以指数级增长。一个原本 6 步的线性流程，加上各种异常路径后，可能膨胀到 40+ 个状态。

    解法是 ：把复杂工作流拆成子工作流，每个子工作流有自己的状态机，父工作流只管理子工作流之间的转移。分层状态机

    陷阱 3：证据验证变成了形式主义

    状态机要求每个状态转移时提交证据，但如果证据验证太松，Agent 就会学会"应付检查"——生成一份看起来像回事但实际上没用的证据。

    我们见过一个案例：Agent 在验证步骤提交了一个 类型的证据，payload 是 。状态机的 gate 检查了 ，就放行了。但实际的测试根本没跑。

    陷阱 4：重试风暴

    当一个步骤失败并触发重试时，如果上游有多个实例同时重试，可能形成"重试风暴"——所有实例在同一时刻对同一个下游服务发起请求。

    陷阱 5：工作流版本管理的缺失

    这是最容易被忽视的陷阱。工作流定义修改了（比如新增了一个验证步骤），但还有 50 个正在进行中的工作流实例运行的是旧版本。新版本部署后，这些实例从 checkpoint 恢复时，发现状态机结构变了，直接崩溃。

    决策框架：什么时候用状态机，什么时候不用

    不是所有 Agent 任务都适合状态机管理。过度工程化同样有害。

    适合状态机的场景：

  • 流程步骤确定，可以提前枚举
  • 步骤之间有明确的先后依赖
  • 失败的代价高（支付、数据删除、外部通知）
  • 需要审计日志和合规记录
  • 多步骤的 CRUD 操作链

    • 不适合状态机的场景：

  • 探索性研究（"帮我调研 XX 领域的最新进展"）
  • 开放式头脑风暴
  • 调试和问题诊断（失败模式未知）
  • 单步骤的简单任务
  • 需要 Agent 自主决定流程走向的创新任务

    • 一个实用的判断标准：如果你能画出这个任务的工作流图，它就适合状态机管理；如果你画不出来，就别硬画。

    可观测性：工作流引擎不是黑盒

    工作流引擎的每一步都应该产生可观测性数据。三个关键指标：

    1. 状态转移延迟（State Transition Latency）

    每个状态的平均停留时间。如果某个状态的 p99 延迟突然飙升，说明这个步骤的下游可能出了问题。

    metrics.(, duration, {
  : workflowId,
  : state.,
  : workflowVersion,
});
histogram'workflow.state_duration_ms'workflow_idstatenameversion

    2. 转移成功率（Transition Success Rate）

    每个状态的转移成功/失败比例。如果某个状态的成功率低于阈值，触发告警。

    3. Checkpoint 大小增长率（Checkpoint Growth Rate）

    如果 checkpoint 数据增长过快，说明 context 在膨胀，可能需要做 context 裁剪。我们见过一个案例，checkpoint 从 2KB 增长到 12MB，导致恢复时间从毫秒级变成秒级。

    写在最后

    Agent 工作流引擎不是一个新概念——传统工作流引擎（Airflow、Temporal、Camunda）已经存在了很多年。但 Agent 时代的工作流引擎需要解决一个传统引擎不需要面对的问题：。执行者（LLM）是非确定性的

    传统工作流引擎假设每个步骤的执行结果是确定的（给定相同的输入）。Agent 不是。同一个 Prompt、同一个上下文，Agent 可能产出不同的结果。这意味着工作流引擎的 gate 验证、证据检查、重试策略都需要为这种不确定性做额外设计。

    2026 年的趋势很明确：Agent 工作流正在从"Prompt 描述"走向"代码强制"。LangGraph 提供了图结构，Temporal 提供了持久化执行，新兴方案提供了可验证执行。选择哪个取决于你的场景复杂度、可靠性要求和团队技术栈。

    但无论选择哪个方向，核心原则不变：流程应该在代码里，而不是在 Prompt 的想象里。

    参考来源：

  • Aharness (GitHub): 工作流的有限状态机实现
  • LangGraph 文档：Graph-based agent orchestration
  • Temporal 文档：Durable execution for long-running workflows
  • Developer's Digest: "Agent Workflows as Code: Why State Machines Beat Prompt Checklists" (2026-06)
  • LangChain Blog: "How to Build a Custom Agent Harness" (2026)

item.title: 清华特奖得主AI创业再+1：GeoPT一作入局物理世界模型
item.description:
来源：量子位（中文） 相关度：13.6 正文：1982 字 / 7 图

命中：世界模型

从搭载物理建模能力的世界模型切入

< img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400">

清华特奖得主AI创业再+1：GeoPT一作入局物理世界模型

梦晨2026-10-1620:54:54 来源：量子位

从搭载物理建模能力的世界模型切入

衡宇 发自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公众号QbitAI

世界模型赛道仍在源源不断涌入最智慧的大脑。

量子位获悉，。曾在2022年获清华特奖的吴海旭，已于今年悄然开启世界模型创业

公司名为物原科技，迄今为止迅速完成了多轮融资，公司估值来到数亿美元，投资方队伍中出现了蚂蚁、美团、达晨财智、星连等一线投资机构的的身影。

今年2月，在技术领域引起热议。吴海旭为一作的工作GeoPT

该工作提出了一种全新的动力学提升预训练范式，通过合成动力学（Synthetic Dynamics）将静态几何“提升”到动态空间，让模型在无标签数据上通过学习粒子轨迹演化来获取物理直觉。

该论文的作者中还出现了清华软件学院长聘副教授（吴海旭博士导师）、MIT，以及MIT教授（吴海旭博士后所在项目组导师）等人。龙明盛何恺明Wojciech Matusik

我们获悉，吴海旭此次创业，选择从切入。搭载物理建模能力的世界模型

据接近物原科技的知情人士透露，该方案一定程度上在技术思路方面延续了GeoPT的研究路线。

吴海旭是谁？

吴海旭于2016年进入清华大学软件学院软件工程专业就读本科，并于次年起在清华数学科学系纯数学与应用数学攻读第二学位。

2019年暑期，他曾作为访问学生进入哈佛大学Visual Computing Group开展研究，导师为教授Hanspeter Pfister。

本科毕业后，他在清华大学软件学院开始了自己的研究生生涯，导师为副教授龙明盛。

龙明盛课题组早期研究迁移学习（Transfer Learning），后来重点转向时序基础模型、时空预测、AI for Science、多模态世界模型等等。

2022年，吴海旭获得了清华的特等奖学金。

清华特奖的含金量大家应该多少有所耳闻，月之暗面杨植麟、OpenAI陈立杰、谷歌姚顺宇（江湖传言其已离职，创业RSI）、Sand.ai曹越、LiberAI刘松铭等都曾获得该奖项。

特奖答辩时，吴海旭就已经在ICML、NeurIPS、IEEE TPAMI等CCF-A类会议/期刊上发表论文7篇，其中一作/共一6篇。

，该工作首次系统性地将序列分解思想与改进的注意力机制深度融合，被称为长时序预测（LSTF）里程碑模型。当时他的核心研究成果是Autoformer

Autoformer后，他又发表了PredRNN、 Corrformer、Transolver、GeoPT等工作。

2025年起，他，GeoPT正是这一时期他的代表性工作。前往MIT CSAIL从事博士后工作

这期间，吴海旭的博士后导师Wojciech Matusik是计算设计与制造领域的知名学者。他的研究横跨计算机图形学、计算制造、机器人学等多个方向，致力于用算法连接数字世界与物理制造。

吴海旭现在的个人主页上注明，其个人的。研究重点主要面向深度学习与科学机器学习，目标是为物理系统构建可扩展原则

其研究聚焦物理系统与动力系统两大主题，主要分为以下三个方向：

基于物理原理的可扩展骨干网络（Autoformer、Corrformer、Transolver）

端到端物理基础模型（TimesNet、Unisolver、GeoPT）

领域感知型科学学习系统（Flowformer、Transolver++、FlashBias）

截至目前，吴海旭的。谷歌学术被引用数为29611

参考链接：[1]https://wuhaixu2016.github.io/[2]https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=oLL_x0wAAAAJ&hl=en[3]https://people.csail.mit.edu/wojciech/[4]https://www.thss.tsinghua.edu.cn/info/1023/2032.htm
